note: AssetClass exists with 5 classes; needs ENGINEERING_EVIDENCE / CUSTOMER_INFORMATION / CONVERSION_CREATIVE / PHYSICAL_PROOF semantics
title: Separate Evidence Assets from Conversion Assets

body: Every asset passes four independent gates before customer use: DATA_TRUTH (values match CIR/gauge/version), LAYOUT_QA (no clipping, overflow, overlap, illegible type or contradictory dimensions), COMMERCIAL_QA (the frame has a defined conversion job and is competitive at mobile/search-grid scale), and POLICY_PROVENANCE (asset type/disclosure/rights satisfy current marketplace rules). Failure at any gate prevents listing export.
note: check_frame_plan + check_assets cover DATA_TRUTH and some LAYOUT_QA; no COMMERCIAL_QA or POLICY_PROVENANCE gate
title: Listing Asset Promotion Gates

body: Add deterministic bounding-box and safe-area tests for title truncation, chart/text collision, footer overlap, edge clipping, minimum font size, mobile crop, aspect ratio and whitespace. Render every listing frame at target Etsy dimensions and at a small mobile preview. Text or charts crossing reserved regions is a test failure, not an aesthetic opinion.
note: LISTING_NO_FONT, LISTING_HERO_FABRIC_FLAT and the thumbnail check exist; no bounding-box/safe-area/mobile-crop suite
title: Automated Visual Layout QA

body: Every displayed measurement must trace to one canonical measurement object. Detect contradictory or contextless dimensions such as a finished-size card showing 90×122 cm alongside an unexplained 180 cm marker. Labels must identify width, length, circumference, component, blocked state and size variant where relevant.
note: geometry.py is the canonical measurement object and refuses what it cannot measure; no cross-frame dimensional consistency auditor
title: Dimensional Consistency Auditor

body: The system must test whether an image communicates what its caption/title claims. A finished-result frame cannot be only abstract horizontal rows. A chart preview must look like a chart preview. A size card must communicate scale clearly. Use independent visual review plus deterministic metadata assertions; do not rely on the generator grading itself.
note: visual semantic QA -- does the image communicate its caption's claim
title: Visual Semantic QA

body: The hero's job is desire and instant comprehension, not documentation. It should communicate the expected finished project at search-grid/mobile scale while remaining truthful and policy-compliant. Technical charts, stitch maps and size cards belong later in the listing sequence unless market evidence proves otherwise.
note: hero rules exist (not a concept, fabric not flat); no finished-project comprehension standard
title: Hero Image Standard

body: Required flow: CIR -> compiled/twin truth -> engineering evidence -> creative brief constrained by truth -> conversion creative -> independent Asset Truth comparison -> layout/commercial/policy gates -> listing export. Creative systems may improve presentation but may never invent motifs, dimensions, texture, construction or included deliverables.
note: the CIR->twin->evidence half is built; no creative brief or conversion creative stage
title: Evidence-to-Creative Pipeline

body: For products initially marketed with permitted non-physical representations, create an automatic upgrade task when tester/customer physical photography becomes available. Replace or supplement weaker conceptual assets with genuine finished-project proof where rights permit, then measure CTR/conversion impact.
note: physical proof upgrade path
title: Physical Proof Upgrade Path

body: Every frame has exactly one primary commercial job: DESIRE, SCALE, DETAIL, CONTENTS, DIFFICULTY, MATERIALS, SIZING, PATTERN_PREVIEW, PROOF or CROSS_SELL. Frames without a buyer-relevant job are removed. Prevent five technically different images from communicating essentially the same thing.
note: six frames have roles; not a one-primary-job map with filler removal
title: Listing Frame Job Map

body: Evaluate every listing set as a shopper actually sees it: search thumbnail, phone gallery, first 3 frames, then full gallery. Store screenshots/renders of these contexts during QA. Optimize title-safe area and visual hierarchy for small screens rather than desktop-only output.
note: thumbnail evaluated at 2000px search scale; no phone gallery or first-3-frames context renders
title: Mobile-First Creative QA

body: Before release, compare the listing set against a current sample of strong products in the same micro-market on measurable dimensions: finished-result clarity, thumbnail stop-power, proof, information density, consistency, video/support proposition and visual polish. Do not copy competitor creative; use the benchmark to reject obviously substandard presentation.
note: competitive creative benchmark needs browser/vision
title: Competitive Creative Benchmark

body: Track clipping, confusing dimensions, misleading visualization, weak hero, unreadable chart and redundant frames as named defect classes. Every production-discovered visual defect gets a regression fixture, just like compiler defects. Asset-system quality should improve monotonically rather than rediscovering the same layout failures.
note: B-084/085/086 became regression fixtures; no named visual defect classes
title: Creative Defect Feedback Loop

body: Internal and customer-facing labeling must distinguish a digital pattern render/chart from a photograph of a physically completed object whenever that distinction is material. Do not use a disclaimer as permission to make a misleading hero; honesty labels complement, not replace, truthful presentation.
note: B-097 labels generated lifestyle imagery; not generalised
title: Technical Asset Honesty Label

body: Create a listing-set certificate tied to product/version that records the exact approved asset hashes, frame order, measurement sources, provenance, disclosures, QA results and policy version. Any product revision that changes geometry/claims invalidates affected listing assets until re-certified. BRAMBLELOOP QUEUED MASTER UPGRADES v1.3.4 - Creative Parity + Model Hard Gate Release-blocking standard: Brambleloop will not accept listing presentation below strong category-matched Etsy benchmarks, and the approved fictional Brambleloop model is mandatory where human modeling is commercially appropriate.
note: listing set release certificate
title: Listing Set Release Certificate

body: Brambleloop does not ship customer-facing listing creative that is materially weaker than the strongest current listings in the same Etsy micro-market. Technical correctness, completed rendering, or internal approval does not satisfy this gate. If a blind side-by-side review would make Brambleloop look amateur, synthetic, confusing or obviously inferior, the listing remains blocked.
note: creative parity gate needs current benchmark evidence (browser)
title: Creative Parity Is a Release-Blocking Gate

body: For appropriate wearables and model-led accessories, the approved fictional Brambleloop adult model is mandatory in the customer-facing gallery unless Policy Gate or product context specifically rules it out. Maintain one recognizable identity across listings: stable facial structure, light eyes, dark brunette hair, approximate age, proportions and editorial character. Wardrobe, pose, season and environment may vary. Material identity drift is a QA failure.
note: Brambleloop model: needs an image generation capability and owner identity selection (199/200)
title: Mandatory Brambleloop Model for Applicable Products

body: Maintain a versioned approved reference pack and character bible containing canonical face views, hair/eye descriptors, proportions, makeup range, expression range, wardrobe rules, lighting language and rejected drift examples. Every new model asset is compared against this pack before approval. Updating the canonical identity is an explicit brand-version event, not accidental generation drift.
note: Brambleloop model: needs an image generation capability and owner identity selection (199/200)
title: Model Continuity Reference Pack

body: Do not force the model into products where she reduces clarity. Blankets, amigurumi, baskets, runners, pillows, ornaments, nursery decor and similar categories should normally lead with the finished project in an aspirational truthful environment. The Model Gate applies only where human modeling materially helps the buyer understand or desire the product.
note: Brambleloop model: needs an image generation capability and owner identity selection (199/200)
title: Product-First Exceptions

body: Before listing export, independently pass: (1) IDENTITY - correct Brambleloop model where applicable; (2) PRODUCT TRUTH - crochet shown matches certified design; (3) HERO - immediate finished-result comprehension; (4) MOBILE GRID - strong at Etsy search-thumbnail scale; (5) LIFESTYLE QUALITY - premium lighting/composition/material realism; (6) GALLERY - complete purposeful sequence without filler; (7) BRAND - recognizably Brambleloop; (8) COMPETITIVE BLIND REVIEW - not materially inferior beside current benchmark listings. Any failure blocks release.
note: Brambleloop model: needs an image generation capability and owner identity selection (199/200)
title: Eight-Part Creative Parity Gate

body: Creative Director maintains a dated benchmark set from strong legitimate listings in each target micro-market. Wearables compare with wearables; mosaic blankets with comparable blankets; amigurumi with comparable amigurumi. Benchmark dimensions include thumbnail clarity, realism, styling, crop, lighting, product prominence, gallery storytelling, information cards, video/support proposition and brand consistency. Learn standards, never copy protected expression.
note: benchmark set must be current; needs browser/vision
title: Benchmark Set Must Be Current and Category-Matched

body: The autonomous system may not lower the visual standard because an asset was AI-assisted. If the available generator cannot achieve benchmark quality and product truth simultaneously, route to a stronger permitted model/tool, change the composition, use deterministic/physical proof, or block the asset. 'Best the current model could do' is not a release criterion.
note: enforced by the ladder having no rung that accepts a weaker image, and by the exhausted-ladder outcome being 'hold the listing'.
title: No AI Quality Discount

body: The gallery must first create desire and comprehension, then substantiate the purchase. Hero/lifestyle frames sell the truthful finished outcome; later evidence frames prove dimensions, chart quality, materials, included files and support. Never use technical evidence as a substitute for aspirational merchandising, and never use aspirational imagery to override evidence.
note: frames carry a declared job and are judged by it: conversion creative on grid readability and physical realism, engineering evidence on agreement with the twin. A gallery of only evidence is a specification sheet nobody clicks; only creative is a listing that converts and then refunds; and an evidence frame in first position is refused.
title: Hero Dream / Evidence Proof Principle

body: Independent visual QA checks stitch-scale plausibility, yarn continuity, edge construction, drape, joins, hands/fingers where present, garment fit, shadows, repeated textures, impossible seams and other synthetic artifacts. Product Truth validates structure; realism QA validates that the customer-facing depiction does not look fake or physically impossible.
note: ten physical-realism checks, and unmade checks on a generated frame are unjudged rather than assumed fine. Remaining: making them, which needs the vision capability.
title: Physical Realism and Crochet Plausibility Review

body: Do not fill a gallery to reach an arbitrary image count. Every frame must pass its commercial job and quality gate. A shorter excellent gallery is preferable to a longer gallery containing weak filler; expand only when additional frames answer a buyer question, add proof or increase desire.
note: every frame must carry a commercial job or it is refused as filler; a frame with no declared job cannot be constructed.
title: Gallery Minimum Quality, Not Minimum Count

body: When Creative Parity fails: regenerate with constrained brief -> change composition/environment -> change permitted image model/tool -> use stronger deterministic representation -> acquire tester/physical proof -> hold listing. Never solve a failed parity gate by relaxing the threshold.
note: six-rung escalation ladder in cost order, ending at hold_listing. Lowering the standard is not a rung, and the exhausted case says so explicitly: #77 is that the bar does not drop because an asset was AI-assisted, so the remaining option is not to publish.
title: Creative Failure Escalation Ladder

body: After launch, measure search-grid CTR, first-frame engagement where available, listing conversion and creative experiment outcomes by asset style. High-performing creative patterns become brand knowledge, but performance never overrides Product Truth, policy or identity continuity. BRAMBLELOOP QUEUED MASTER UPGRADES v1.3.5 - Creativity Engine + Autonomous Continuous Improvement Added after comparing early generated concepts with current market creative. This upgrade makes product desirability a pre-engineering gate and establishes a permanent, controlled self-improvement organization so Brambleloop compounds knowledge and capability instead of remaining static.
note: creative performance learning; needs launch data
title: Creative Performance Learning

body: A technically feasible concept does not deserve CIR engineering merely because it fills a keyword/category slot. Before expensive engineering, independently score visual hook, emotional hook, functional hook, distinctiveness, giftability/occasion fit, thumbnail concept, collection potential, physical plausibility and competitive novelty. Concepts below threshold are killed or returned for ideation.
note: creative/jury.py is a pre-engineering hard gate whose best verdict without a vision model is needs_taste, never approved: structural critics are real and cannot tell whether a thing is desirable, so a concept reaching engineering on structural cleanliness alone is exactly what this requirement forbids.
title: Design Desirability Is a Pre-Engineering Hard Gate

body: For each commercially promising opportunity, generate a diverse field of materially different concepts before selecting one. Target approximately 12-25 concepts when economics justify it. Do not accept superficial colour/name variants as diversity. The tournament should include different forms, transformations, storage/presentation ideas, motif systems, emotional tones, construction approaches and bundle/collection possibilities.
note: the field is judged before any concept in it. 12-25 required, and a field whose mean pairwise distance falls below the spread minimum is refused as 'one idea in N costumes' with the near-identical pairs named. Palette is deliberately not a term in the distance function, so a recolour scores 0.0 against its original.
title: Creative Concept Tournament

body: Create a Creativity Director responsible for concept quality, plus independent critic agents that attack sameness, genericness, weak emotional appeal, derivative thinking, poor thumbnail potential and unnecessary complexity. The proposing agent may not be the sole judge of its own concept. Jury feedback becomes structured training memory for future ideation.
note: six independent critics attacking sameness, genericness, weak emotional appeal, derivative thinking, thumbnail potential and unnecessary complexity. Each can only reject -- a scoring jury averages the fatal objection away, the same arithmetic mistake as averaging the confidence ladder. One rejection ends the concept.
title: Creativity Director + Adversarial Creative Jury

body: Continuously study legitimate current market examples across categories to learn abstract commercial attributes: clever transformation, strong silhouette, recognisable motif, cute characterisation, premium minimalism, gift narrative, modularity, low-sew appeal, surprising function and collection logic. Store attributes and outcomes, not copied protected expression.
note: creativity benchmark memory; needs market observation
title: Creativity Benchmark Memory

body: Before engineering, compare a candidate against observed competitor concepts and Brambleloop's own catalogue. Reject near-clones, trivial recolours and ideas whose primary appeal depends on reproducing another seller's distinctive expression. Require a defensible Brambleloop creative contribution.
note: novelty distance against both our own catalogue and observed benchmark concepts, with a clone threshold tuned against the pair this company already has. Entering the same broad arena stays explicitly allowed (#215, #306); what is refused is a concept whose distinctiveness collapses to one seller's execution.
title: Novelty Distance / Anti-Clone Gate

body: Every finalist must have a one-sentence visual premise and a thumbnail storyboard before CIR work. Ask: if seller name, reviews, badges and price vanished, would the product idea itself still create curiosity or desire at mobile-grid size? If not, return to ideation.
note: a one-sentence visual premise is required at construction time, and a premise built only from generic tokens is refused by the genericness critic: if the seller name, price and reviews vanished, nothing in it would create curiosity. The thumbnail critic catches small objects whose appeal is fine detail.
title: Idea-to-Thumbnail Test

body: After launch, connect concept attributes to real outcomes: impressions, CTR, favourites, conversion, reviews, repeat purchase, support burden and contribution. Learn which kinds of originality create demand for Brambleloop. Do not equate novelty with success; optimize useful/desirable originality.
note: creativity outcome learning; needs launch data
title: Creativity Outcome Learning

body: Create a permanent autonomous Improvement Department whose only mission is to make Brambleloop and every department measurably better over time. It observes incidents, experiments, customer feedback, market changes, agent performance, cost, latency, product quality, creative quality and commercial outcomes; proposes bounded improvements; tests them; and promotes only evidence-backed upgrades.
note: improve/ is the department. Its central risk is why governance.py exists: every number this company reports is produced by a check, so the cheapest way to improve any of them is to weaken the check that produces it.
title: Continuous Improvement Department

body: Each major department receives an improvement cell: Product Creativity, Pattern Engineering, QA, Market Radar, Pricing, Creative Assets, SEO/Search, Growth/Ads, Customer Experience, Portfolio, Finance and Runtime. Cells maintain their own defect/opportunity backlog, experiments, baselines and improvement history while a central Improvement Director prevents conflicting local optimizations.
note: twelve cells, one per department, each owning a single metric AND the statement of where the number comes from -- a rating a cell assigns itself is not a measurement, so every cell names its source in rows.
title: Department Improvement Cells

body: Self-improvement follows a controlled loop: observe evidence -> identify constraint -> form explicit hypothesis -> implement in sandbox/branch -> run regression/adversarial tests -> compare against baseline -> promote if better -> monitor -> rollback if worse -> record lesson. Production code/prompts/rules may not self-modify blindly.
note: observe -> hypothesise -> sandbox -> test -> promote -> monitor. The baseline is captured at proposal time, never after: a result compared against a number measured afterwards is compared with itself, which makes every promotion a success and the loop decorative. A first measurement becomes the baseline rather than a win.
title: Learn -> Hypothesize -> Sandbox -> Test -> Promote Loop

body: Every promoted improvement stores previous version, test evidence, expected metric effect and rollback path. If post-promotion quality, cost, reliability, policy compliance or commercial KPI materially degrades, automatically revert within defined authority. Safety/policy/financial gates cannot be weakened by the learning system.
note: a rollback reference is required before a hypothesis can be recorded, and monitor() reverts a degrading promotion automatically rather than escalating it -- a regression that waits to be agreed is a regression that stays deployed over a weekend. The post-promotion observation is kept either way.
title: Immutable Baselines and Automatic Rollback

body: Track creative capability over time using blinded human/agent benchmark comparisons, concept diversity, novelty distance, desirability scores, percentage of concepts surviving the tournament, market CTR/conversion, winner rate and repeated-theme fatigue. The objective is demonstrable improvement in idea quality, not simply more generated ideas.
note: creative/tournament.scorecard() tracks field spread, survival rate, death causes and their trends, and refuses to read a rising survival rate alongside falling spread as progress -- a jury going soft looks identical to improvement on survival alone. Everything computable without a model is computed. What remains is the blinded human/agent benchmark comparison, which needs a model to be the agent side, and market CTR, which needs live traffic. Parked on model_provider rather than left in the ready queue as work nobody can start.
title: Creativity Capability Scorecard

body: Score agents and prompt/model configurations on domain-specific outcomes, cost and reliability. Run challenger configurations against incumbents on controlled tasks. Promote challengers only when they beat the incumbent without violating truth/policy gates. Retire persistently weak configurations.
note: improve/league.py runs challengers against incumbents on a fixed shared task set, refuses a challenger judged on tasks it introduced, scores quality, cost and reliability together with the cost bar scaling with the ratio, and routes promotion through the improvement boundary
title: Agent Performance League

body: Version every material prompt, model, tool and decision policy. Record why it changed, tests, cost, measured outcome and affected departments. Improvement agents may recommend switching providers/tools when evidence supports it, subject to existing owner spend/credential gates.
note: ConfigVersion records every prompt, model, tool and policy version with why it changed, the tests run, its cost and the departments it affects; an incumbent with no measured outcome is reported as running because it was first
title: Prompt / Model / Tool Evolution Registry

body: A lesson discovered in one department must be routable to others. Example: customers strongly prefer low-sew construction -> Market Radar scores low-sew opportunities higher, Creativity explores low-sew concepts, Pattern Engineering prioritizes suitable primitives, Listings surface the benefit, and Support tracks whether it reduces confusion.
note: improve/bus.py routes a lesson by its subject rather than to a maintained distribution list, and a subject with no audience is refused: a lesson nobody receives changes nothing. A cell that was never sent a lesson cannot claim to have acted on it.
title: Cross-Department Lesson Bus

body: Continuously monitor permitted sources for new crochet techniques, aesthetics, seasonal behaviour, marketplace tooling/policy, search changes, image/video capabilities, competitor positioning and customer pain points. Every observation stores source/date/freshness and is separated from verified internal causal evidence.
note: intel/learning.py holds the eight domains the requirement names, each with its own freshness window -- a marketplace policy ages in three weeks and a stitch technique does not age at all -- and refuses an observation with no source, no citation or no date. The second clause is the load-bearing one and is mechanical: observations are stored apart from internal lessons, carry kind=external_signal, as_evidence() refuses by name, and support() refuses a signal passed in the evidence list. A claim may rest on signals alone and says so. A domain nobody has looked at is named rather than counted as zero. Remaining: nothing fetches these yet, so every domain currently reports unobserved, which the radar states plainly. /api/learning.
title: External Learning Radar

body: Continuous learning is not permission to burn unlimited tokens or rebuild working systems. Track improvement cost and expected/realized benefit. Prioritize changes with high expected impact on product desirability, quality, conversion, acquisition, margin or reliability. Apply stagnation/thrash rules to the Improvement Department itself.
note: improve/roi.py reads realised benefit against the baseline captured at proposal time, and deliberately does not read the sandbox result that won the promotion as its return -- counting it would make every promotion succeed by construction. A promotion younger than the realisation window is too_early rather than a failure; one older with nothing measured since is a cost with no return. prioritise() refuses a candidate that cannot say in advance what would count as it having worked. /api/roi.
title: Improvement Budget and ROI

body: On a scheduled cadence, the Improvement Director produces an internal machine-readable retrospective: what improved, what regressed, what was learned, current bottleneck, experiments completed, experiments killed, department health, top next upgrades and STOP-doing list. It should execute approved low-risk improvements rather than merely write reports.
note: the weekly retrospective reports what regressed as prominently as what improved, names the bottleneck, and counts the cells that have no measurement at all -- improvement in those is unclaimable rather than unproven. Scheduled as a weekly cadence.
title: Weekly Autonomous Business Retrospective

body: Brambleloop must not repeatedly start from generic model intelligence. Persist structured lessons from every product, competitor scan, experiment, incident, support case and sale. New designs should demonstrably use accumulated Brambleloop knowledge while remaining original. The expected creative bar rises as the evidence base grows.
note: improve/roi.design_provenance records which accumulated lessons a specific new design drew on, refusing a citation of a lesson the company does not have; compounding_report() reports the share of designs standing on accumulated knowledge and says restarting-from-generic-intelligence by name when that share is zero. Unmeasurable until designs record it, rather than reported as zero. /api/roi.
title: Compounding Knowledge Requirement

body: The system may autonomously improve code, prompts, scoring, workflows and agent configuration within tested, reversible and spend-authorized bounds. It may never autonomously weaken policy gates, fabricate evidence/reviews, bypass owner-only legal/KYC/spend gates, erase audit history, or promote an untested change directly to production.
note: governance.check() refuses at proposal time, before any work is done: weakening a protected gate, fabricating evidence, widening the system's own authority, irreversibility, and spending past the improvement budget. A hypothesis cannot evade it by declaring no surfaces. The boundary is also stated in prose on /api/improve, because a boundary only the code knows is one the owner cannot hold anybody to.
title: Self-Improvement Governance Boundary

body: Claims such as circle, oval, square, hexagon, tapered, fitted, spherical, conical or panel geometry must be computationally derivable from certified construction data where applicable. Customer text, charts, twin geometry and CIR must agree. A metadata label alone is not evidence that the pattern produces the claimed shape.
note: cir/geometry.py + gates/asset_truth.check_shape_claims; B-059/061/103 is exactly this gate, derived from certified construction
title: Geometry Truth / Visual Shape Gate

body: The long-term creative objective is explicit: later Brambleloop concepts should be more desirable, distinctive and commercially informed than earlier ones. Improvement is measured against historical Brambleloop cohorts and current category benchmarks. If creative capability plateaus, the Improvement Department treats that as a top-level business defect. BRAMBLELOOP QUEUED MASTER UPGRADES v1.3.6 - Deep Seasonal Creativity Audit This audit was derived from the supplied Etsy benchmark screenshots. The observed standard is not merely attractive photography: strong products repeatedly combine recognizable silhouettes, dimensional motifs, functional transformations, gift narratives, character systems, seasonal storytelling and cohesive model-led merchandising. Brambleloop must treat that level as a floor and seek original concepts beyond it.
note: the north star is explicit in the scorecard and distinctiveness is measured against historical cohorts. What remains is desirability, which is a judgement no code here can make and no data here supports, and the commercial half, which needs the benchmark scan. Parked on model_provider.
title: Creative Growth North Star

body: Replace narrow holiday keyword generation with a permanent Seasonal Creative Universe. Every holiday, season and gift occasion maintains an evolving taxonomy of product forms, motifs, emotions, recipients, rooms/use contexts, skill levels, make-times, price bands and gifting narratives. Christmas alone must span stockings, ornaments, wreaths, tree skirts, garlands, advent pieces, tableware, kitchen decor, blankets, pillows, baskets, gift bags, amigurumi, wearables, nursery, pet, door decor and original hybrids.
note: creative/universe.UNIVERSE holds a department taxonomy per occasion -- sixteen for Christmas -- and cells() crosses it with eighteen contexts, so a brief is generated against a cell rather than a keyword
title: Seasonal Creative Universe

body: For every seasonal opportunity, deliberately combine two or more dimensions that do not normally appear together: motif x function, holiday x storage, character x household utility, wearable x personalization, amigurumi x organization, decor x interaction, nursery x keepsake, tableware x character, modularity x gifting. The purpose is to create new product premises rather than another recoloured commodity.
note: creative/invention.cross() requires two dimensions that do not normally co-occur and refuses a self-pairing or two near-synonyms; matrix() holds #106's nine named pairings as a queue of empty brief slots
title: Cross-Category Invention Matrix

body: Study the strongest market examples for transformation logic: a pumpkin that becomes/coexists with coasters, a flower that becomes a functional table object, a stocking built from modular squares, a plant pot turned into a holiday character scene, cutlery holders turned into Santa/reindeer/tree characters. Learn the abstract transformation pattern, never the seller's protected expression, then invent original transformations.
note: invention.transform() holds nine abstract transformation patterns and refuses a description that names a specific seller's product -- the same content boundary the teardown library uses
title: Form Transformation Engine

body: At mobile-grid scale, the product should have a recognisable silhouette or visual structure whenever the category permits. Generic circles, rectangles and tubes require an exceptional texture, motif, transformation or use-case to survive. A concept that needs its title to explain why it is interesting is weak.
note: invention.silhouette() knows which forms are shapes rather than outlines and enforces #108's own sentence literally: the premise is read with the title's words removed
title: Product Silhouette Gate

body: Creative generation must explicitly choose and execute an emotional promise: magical, nostalgic, whimsical, cozy, elegant, funny, adorable, heirloom, rustic, modern, playful, premium, surprising or gift-worthy. The emotional promise must be visible in the object itself, not merely added as listing copy.
note: invention.promise() requires the feeling to be delivered by a physical execution and refuses listing copy as a mechanism
title: Emotional Design Vocabulary

body: Maintain a broad motif grammar per season without collapsing into cliches. Christmas includes trees, stockings, bows, candy, gingerbread, snow, woodland, stars, ornaments, Santa, reindeer, wreaths and more; fall includes leaves, mushrooms, acorns, pumpkins, woodland and harvest; Halloween includes ghosts, bats, monsters, witches and haunted architecture; spring/Easter includes florals, chicks, rabbits, eggs and garden life. Agents must recombine, stylize and abstract motifs into original Brambleloop design language.
note: invention.MOTIF_GRAMMAR holds 10-20 motifs per season, SATURATED names the clichés, and a selection built only from them is reported as the commodity by construction
title: Seasonal Motif Grammar

body: Before engineering a strong seasonal concept, ask whether it can seed a coherent family: hero product, quick-make companion, bundle, giftable mini, decor variant, wearable/accessory or adjacent room/use case. Prefer ideas that can become collections without forcing low-quality derivatives.
note: creative/family.py runs the family test before engineering, on structure rather than enthusiasm: five roles with the forms that can fill them, a construction -> form buildability map and a construction -> size-band range, so a role is viable only when the hero's own visual idea survives the size change and the form can actually be built that way. Size compatibility alone would invent members -- an amigurumi robin and a scarf are both small objects -- which is the derivative-forcing the requirement names, reached from the other side. A concept that fails is reported as a single product, not refused, and a bundle is derived from two viable roles rather than asserted. /api/seasonal/capacity.
title: Multi-Product Family Test

body: Creative scoring must account for how long the buyer needs to make the item. Large blankets and complex garments must enter the market much earlier than ornaments/coasters/quick gifts. Seasonal Radar should shift late-window capacity toward fast makes instead of continuing to design products customers no longer have time to complete.
note: creative/family.window_fit grades a concept's make lane against the time left, using the make-time interval rather than a point estimate: infeasible means the optimistic bound has passed and everything short of it carries a real multiplier because hurry and stop are different instructions. Wired into creative scoring as the jury's shopping_window critic, which judges nothing when nobody said how long is left -- an unknown window is not a comfortable one -- and into the autopsy's diagnosis. shift_capacity() names what to continue, what to hurry and what to stand down, and the heaviest lane new work should use.
title: Make-Time / Shopping-Window Creative Fit

body: Generate seasonal concepts against explicit recipient/context cells: adult self-use, host gift, child, baby/nursery, teacher, coworker, pet owner, family tradition, stocking stuffer, table setting, fireplace, tree, front door, kitchen, bedroom, office, cottage and party. This expands demand discovery beyond generic 'Christmas crochet pattern'.
note: universe.CONTEXTS is #113's own list of people and places, and coverage() reports depth as cells covered rather than a product count
title: Recipient and Context Matrix

body: Each major seasonal wave should contain intentional beginner/quick-win, intermediate and advanced/heirloom opportunities. Do not let the portfolio become entirely complex flagship work or entirely trivial quick makes. Skill level is part of market segmentation and gifting/make-time strategy.
note: universe.skill_portfolio() measures the three levels against healthy shares: a wave of only flagships has no beginner entry and one of only quick makes has nothing anybody keeps
title: Skill-Level Portfolio

body: Every flagship concept must contain at least one explicit WOW mechanism: surprising transformation, exceptional motif composition, dimensional construction, unusual but useful function, strong character system, modular reveal, personalization architecture, striking texture, premium silhouette or collection-scale storytelling. 'Clean and correct' is not enough.
note: invention.wow() requires a flagship to declare one of ten mechanisms and to ground it in something about the object; an ungrounded mechanism is a checkbox
title: Wow-Factor Requirement

body: When studying high-performing products, decompose why they work into non-copying primitives: silhouette, motif density, dimensionality, palette role, prop/context, function, emotional tone, construction novelty, personalization, bundle logic and thumbnail readability. Store the decomposition, not a replica prompt.
note: creative reference decomposition; needs benchmark observation
title: Creative Reference Decomposition

body: Detect when a concept archetype is overcrowded. If dozens of nearly interchangeable pumpkin coasters, granny stockings or basic wreaths dominate results, Brambleloop must either find a meaningful unmet angle or move to a less saturated creative territory. Popularity alone does not justify imitation.
note: discovery.may_enter() refuses a crowded archetype without a named unmet angle: popularity is evidence it sells and evidence the next one is invisible, and only the second has arithmetic behind it
title: Creative Saturation Detector

body: Create an agent dedicated to asking what buyers plausibly want that current search results do not satisfy. It mines review complaints, missing variants, awkward construction, poor styling, weak personalization, excessive sewing, bad sizing, low giftability and absent combinations. White-space hypotheses feed the Concept Tournament.
note: discovery.white_space() mines eight closed complaint kinds into ranked hypotheses, and reports that it has nothing to mine rather than proposing from the category
title: White-Space Discovery Agent

body: A concept tournament cannot be dominated by one construction or motif. Enforce diversity across product form, function, emotional tone, construction method, motif family, recipient and make-time. The objective is exploration breadth before exploitation.
note: universe.diversity() measures dominance per axis, because breadth in one axis is not breadth and the entrant count is what makes a narrow tournament look wide
title: Creative Diversity Quotas

body: Seasonal learning must transfer abstractly. If modular character pockets convert at Halloween, Christmas/Easter agents may explore the mechanism with original themes. If quick low-sew minis outperform late in a season, future seasonal allocation learns that timing rule. Transfer mechanisms, not designs.
note: discovery.transfer() carries one of seven abstract mechanisms and refuses a design or a reused theme -- the distinction that collapses first under a deadline
title: Holiday-to-Holiday Learning Transfer

body: Maintain Spring, Summer, Fall and Winter creative programs independent of named holidays. Examples include garden/floral, cottage/beach, harvest/woodland, cozy/winter-neutral, home refresh, outdoor entertaining and seasonal wardrobe opportunities. Revenue should not collapse between major holidays.
note: universe.FOUR_SEASON_PROGRAMS holds seven programs across the four seasons, independent of any named holiday
title: Four-Season Engine

body: Continuously explore birthdays, baby showers, nursery, weddings, housewarming, teacher gifts, graduation, pet gifts, hostess gifts and family keepsakes. These provide evergreen/event demand that complements the holiday calendar.
note: universe.NON_HOLIDAY_OCCASIONS holds #122's ten evergreen and event occasions with what each one actually is
title: Non-Holiday Occasion Engine

body: For each occasion, maintain research start, concept freeze, engineering start, physical-test deadline, creative-production deadline, listing/indexing date, promotional ramp, peak window, last practical make date and clearance/evergreen transition. Missed dates are portfolio failures and feed retrospective learning.
note: seasonal/calendar.collection_calendar() holds #123's ten dated milestones per occasion and reports a missed one as a portfolio failure. Run today it finds five of Christmas 2026's ten already past
title: Seasonal Collection Calendar

body: Set a moving minimum creative threshold based on Brambleloop's trailing cohorts and current category benchmarks. A concept that would have passed six months ago can fail today if the company has learned enough to demand better. Continuous improvement must literally raise the release bar.
note: standard.floor() derives the bar from the trailing cohort's median, so a concept that would have passed six months ago can fail today, with an absolute floor underneath so a bad quarter cannot lower it
title: Creativity Floor Rises Over Time

body: Competitive parity is the floor. Flagship creative should target the top decile of current category presentation and concept strength, and experiments should attempt to exceed it. The system should ask 'what would make this the most memorable result on the page?' while preserving originality, truth and feasibility.
note: standard.aspiration() targets the category's ninetieth percentile for flagships and refuses to estimate a decile from fewer than five benchmark scores
title: Top-Decile Aspiration, Not Average Parity

body: Before CIR engineering for expensive concepts and again before release, render concept boards/thumbnails into a simulated Etsy-style grid beside a current category-matched benchmark set with seller/review signals hidden. Independent judges rank attention, comprehension, desire and distinctiveness. Brambleloop must clear the defined threshold without brand favoritism.
note: search-grid blind tournament; needs benchmark evidence
title: Search-Grid Blind Tournament

body: Every rejected or underperforming concept receives a structured autopsy: generic form, weak silhouette, no emotional hook, over-saturated motif, poor function, too complex, wrong timing, weak thumbnail, derivative distance, or merchandising mismatch. These autopsies directly update future ideation constraints.
note: standard.autopsy() records a closed rejection reason with a specific detail, and autopsy_patterns() surfaces when one reason dominates -- which is a brief problem rather than forty concept problems
title: Creative Failure Autopsy

body: When a seasonal product breaks out, decompose the winning mechanism and immediately explore adjacent ORIGINAL opportunities across format, recipient, complexity and bundle position while the window remains open. Do not merely recolour or clone the winner.
note: seasonal breakout mining; needs sales
title: Seasonal Breakout Mining

body: Creative output should be judged as if produced by an elite independent crochet designer and merchandiser, not as 'good for AI'. Agents must be able to reject technically valid ideas as boring, obvious or commercially forgettable. The creativity department is rewarded for hit quality and learning, not concept volume.
note: standard.meets_standard() treats a taste rejection as final: no correctness score overrides 'boring', because the correctness score is exactly what a boring concept passes
title: Human-Quality Creative Standard

body: For model-appropriate products, use the canonical fictional Brambleloop model as a recurring editorial character across seasons, with coherent environments and styling while preserving identity. She may present stockings, wear garments, hold decor or demonstrate scale when commercially useful; she must not obscure product-first clarity.
note: model-led brand storytelling; same model gate
title: Model-Led Brand Storytelling

body: Storefront banners, featured collections, thumbnails, bundles and content should transition ahead of each seasonal buying window. Maintain Brambleloop brand continuity while making the shop feel timely and alive. Seasonal takeovers are scheduled from the Collection Calendar, not improvised after demand peaks.
note: brand/takeover.py schedules the five surfaces from the collection calendar's own milestones rather than from a judgement about how much warning feels right: the featured collection rides listing_indexing_date, the banner and bundles the promotional ramp, shop content and thumbnails the peak window -- because a thumbnail saying December in October competes against what the buyer can still finish. Every takeover carries its revert date, scheduled with its start, since the failure is not the Christmas banner going up late but its still being up in February. Six brand invariants are refused rather than flagged: a shop that resets its wordmark each quarter is not seasonal, it is unrecognisable. A takeover with no event is refused as an ad-hoc change. /api/takeovers.
title: Seasonal Storefront Takeovers

body: Track concept-to-engineering survival, concept-to-launch survival, blind-grid score, novelty distance, CTR, favourite rate, conversion, bestseller incidence, contribution, collection attach rate and creative defect rate by cohort. Improvement Department must show whether creativity is actually getting better. BRAMBLELOOP QUEUED MASTER UPGRADES v1.3.7 - Culture & Nostalgia Opportunity Engine This upgrade expands Brambleloop beyond marketplace-following. The company continuously watches cultural demand and translates strong signals into original, commercially useful crochet opportunities, with a separate clearance lane for direct references when rights permit.
note: standard.north_star() tracks all eleven metrics by cohort and separates the four computable today from the seven that need customers. The seven -- CTR, favourite rate, conversion, bestseller incidence, contribution, collection attach rate and concept-to-launch survival -- stay unmeasurable until there are orders, and are reported as unmeasurable rather than as zero. Nothing executable remains.
title: Creative Department North-Star Metrics

body: Create a permanent radar that scans current and recurring cultural demand around movies, television, memes, nostalgia eras, seasonal traditions, viral aesthetics, music, sports culture, celebrity-driven aesthetics and internet moments. The purpose is early demand discovery: identify what people are emotionally engaging with before Etsy competition fully reflects it.
note: culture/radar.py records signals with their protected tokens declared at observation, keeps momentum as a series, and reports honestly that no feed is connected rather than returning an empty trend list
title: Culture & Nostalgia Radar

body: For every strong signal, decompose the demand into non-protected commercial primitives: emotion, setting, era, humour type, colour language, object category, ritual, character archetype, visual motif class and gifting context. Feed those primitives into Brambleloop's Concept Tournament to invent original crochet products rather than simply reproducing source material.
note: culture/translate.py decomposes into the ten primitives #134 names and check_free_of() proves the protected token did not survive: decomposition nobody checks is a paraphrase
title: Culture-to-Product Translation Engine

body: Maintain a separate lane for public-domain, licensed, permissioned or otherwise cleared material. Direct names, characters, dialogue, logos or distinctive protected expression may enter production only when the rights/policy gate records the basis for use. Unclear rights route to the original-concept lane rather than silently blocking the entire cultural opportunity.
note: culture/rights.py routes unclear rights to the original lane rather than blocking the opportunity, and a direct reference needs a recorded basis with evidence behind it
title: Direct-Reference Clearance Lane

body: Score cultural signals on search momentum, recurrence, nostalgia durability, seasonal fit, crochet translatability, giftability, visual recognisability, product-family potential, competition density, make-time window and rights feasibility. This prevents chasing every meme while still reacting quickly to unusually strong opportunities.
note: culture/score.py scores the eleven components; rights feasibility and the make-time window are gates rather than weights, and an unobserved component is absent rather than zero
title: Cultural Moment Opportunity Score

body: Treat eras as reusable demand territories independent of franchises: retro suburban Christmas, 1980s holiday maximalism, 1990s family Christmas, vintage ski lodge, mid-century holiday, classic storybook winter, retro Halloween, cottage summer and similar aesthetics. Combine era signals with original Brambleloop forms, functions and motifs.
note: translate.ERAS holds nine reusable territories; an era invented per signal is refused because the value of an era is that it recurs
title: Nostalgia Era Engine

body: When a cultural signal is strong, generate a broad set of original translations across blankets, stockings, ornaments, coasters, wreaths, garlands, tableware, amigurumi, wearables, bags, pillows, nursery, pet, kitchen and interactive/transforming products. Require materially different premises and run the same desirability/novelty/grid gates as other concepts.
note: translate.white_space() measures families and distinct premises rather than a count, which is what the jury cannot see reading one at a time
title: Cultural White-Space Tournament

body: Treat famous dialogue, lyrics, slogans and catchphrases as a distinct rights-sensitive asset class. The radar may record them as evidence of the underlying humour or cultural moment, but customer-facing direct use requires clearance. Otherwise generate original language and product concepts expressing the same broad emotional territory without copying the phrase.
note: dialogue, lyrics, slogans and catchphrases are their own rights-sensitive classes in rights.PROTECTED_CLASSES, and check_direct_use() catches one reaching customer-facing output through the original lane
title: Quote / Catchphrase Risk Router

body: Measure how Google/social/search interest precedes or follows Etsy demand by topic and season. Learn which cultural signals are useful leading indicators for crochet products so Brambleloop can enter before saturation rather than after competitors dominate.
note: radar.lead_lag() derives the lead from both series and names the case where the radar is reporting the news. Needs a connected search source and a marketplace source to produce two real series
title: Cultural Demand Lead-Lag Model

body: Create a small autonomous cell for time-sensitive cultural opportunities. It may accelerate research, concept tournament, feasibility and creative prototyping, but it cannot bypass CIR, Product Truth, Creative Parity, policy, spend or release gates. Speed comes from prioritization and parallelism, not lower standards.
note: culture/rapid.py names what may be accelerated and what may never be bypassed as two closed lists, and its forbidden list covers the Improvement Department's protected gates
title: Rapid Response Creative Cell

body: Build durable original territories around recurring cultural emotions: chaotic family holiday, over-the-top decorating, awkward relatives, winter road trip, office holiday party, cozy movie night, magical childhood Christmas, retro toy-shop winter, spooky-cute Halloween, romantic-comedy Valentine mood and similar themes. These become reusable Brambleloop IP rather than dependence on external franchises.
note: translate.THEMES holds ten durable franchise-free territories; a theme invented per signal is refused as a franchise with the name filed off
title: Recurring Franchise-Free Occasion Themes

body: A strong cultural territory should spawn a coherent original collection when justified: flagship, quick-make, giftable mini, decor, wearable/accessory and bundle. Maintain consistent Brambleloop visual language while varying form and price point.
note: translate.collection() reports the six roles' shape rather than declaring a collection from a product count
title: Culture-Informed Collection Architecture

body: Persist every observed signal, source/date, concept translations, rejected ideas, launch outcomes and decay curve. Future agents should know which cultural territories recur annually, which were one-week fads, which translated well into crochet, and which produced poor economics.
note: culture_signals and culture_observations persist every signal, source, exit reason and lesson, are non-rederivable in the continuity export, and memory() names which territories recur annually
title: Cultural Trend Memory

body: Do not keep producing into a cultural trend after the window closes. Detect declining search momentum, rising copycat density, poor CTR/conversion or insufficient remaining make-time. Shift capacity to the next seasonal/cultural wave and record the exit lesson.
note: radar.exit_check() treats any one of declining interest, copycat density, poor conversion or insufficient make time as sufficient, and unmeasured conversion is not read as failure
title: Cultural Saturation & Timing Exit

body: Use cultural observation as raw material to build Brambleloop-owned recurring characters, motifs, jokes, traditions and collection worlds. The long-term goal is not permanent dependence on external pop culture; it is to develop recognizable original seasonal IP that customers return for.
note: translate.owned_territories() makes the borrowed/owned split countable across 19 territories. Recurring Brambleloop characters and collection worlds are not built yet
title: Original Brambleloop Cultural IP

body: Culture & Nostalgia Radar findings flow into Market Radar, Creativity, SEO, Content, Seasonal Planning and Improvement Department. Post-launch outcomes update cultural scoring weights so the system becomes better at distinguishing commercially useful cultural signals from noise. BRAMBLELOOP QUEUED MASTER UPGRADES v1.3.8 - Competitive Product Teardown Laboratory This upgrade adds a controlled post-purchase benchmark laboratory. Purchased competitor files remain a separate benchmark library; Brambleloop learns abstract customer-experience mechanisms and raises its standards without treating competitor patterns as generation source material.
note: cultural_territory and cultural_timing route through the lesson bus to creativity, market radar, SEO and portfolio. Post-launch outcomes updating the scoring weights needs launch data that does not exist
title: Culture Radar Feeds Continuous Improvement

body: Create a permanent laboratory for purchased competitor benchmark products. Its purpose is to study the post-purchase customer experience and raise Brambleloop's standards, not to reuse competitor pattern expression. Purchased files are external benchmark artifacts with restricted access and provenance.
note: teardown/ is the laboratory: library.py quarantines the purchased files, scorecard.py turns them into a standard. The boundary was built before any file arrived, because a boundary added afterwards was absent exactly when it mattered.
title: Competitive Product Teardown Laboratory

body: Keep competitor PDFs, charts, videos and supplemental downloads in a separate BENCHMARK_LIBRARY from Brambleloop generation corpora, CIR primitives and product source data. The generation system must not retrieve competitor row-by-row instructions as reusable pattern content. Derived observations must be abstracted into features, metrics, defects and standards.
note: the library lives outside the repository tree, is in .gitignore, and retrieve() is its only reader -- refusing every generation, listing, support, marketing and publishing role by name with the reason, refusing any role not explicitly an analyst, and refusing a path that resolves outside the library root. Enforced by PermissionError, not by policy.
title: Benchmark Library Separation

body: Every purchased benchmark records seller/shop, product title, category, listing reference, purchase date, paid price, sale state, files received, why selected, visible listing promises, review/reputation context where relevant, and benchmark dimensions. Preserve original filenames and packaging structure.
note: BenchmarkProduct records seller, title, category, pod, listing reference, purchase date, price, sale state, files (name, role, size, sha256), why selected, visible listing promises and benchmark dimensions. Filenames and hashes only -- no row in this system has a column for a competitor's instructions.
title: Benchmark Manifest

body: Compare what the Etsy listing promised with what the customer actually receives: file count, PDF depth, charts, photos, diagrams, video/tutorial links, sizing, materials, skill level, terminology, bonuses, support, printability and update/version information. Score expectation alignment and identify over/under-delivery.
note: promise_audit() compares the listing's promises against what the download actually contains, and judges only what the manifest can settle: promises about sizing depth or troubleshooting quality are reported as unverifiable from filenames rather than guessed, which is the blank-hero mistake this company has already made once.
title: Promise-to-Delivery Audit

body: Analyze cover, table of contents, quick-start, materials, gauge, sizing, abbreviations, technique explanations, construction overview, row/round instructions, charts, assembly, finishing, blocking, troubleshooting, credits, rights/use terms, support and cross-sell. Record information architecture rather than copying prose.
note: audits.PDF_ARCHITECTURE records the nineteen sections #152 enumerates as presence rather than prose: information architecture transfers, the competitor's words never do
title: PDF Information Architecture Teardown

body: Score scanability, repeat notation, row grouping, stitch-count visibility, terminology consistency, size grading, colour-change clarity, assembly clarity and cognitive load. Identify mechanisms that make instructions easier or harder to follow. Convert winning mechanisms into Brambleloop publishing requirements.
note: audits.INSTRUCTION_CLARITY scores the nine mechanisms #153 names, and publishing_requirements() converts each winning one into a Brambleloop requirement to exceed it rather than match it
title: Instruction Clarity Benchmark

body: Evaluate chart legibility, symbols, legends, colour independence, pagination, row numbering, motif boundaries, print quality, scale, schematics, assembly diagrams and correspondence with written instructions. Brambleloop should target clearer charts and stronger written/chart cross-validation than the best benchmark.
note: audits.CHART_BENCHMARK scores all twelve chart elements including colour independence and written/chart correspondence; the derived requirement is to beat the best benchmark, per #154's own wording
title: Chart and Diagram Benchmark

body: Audit assumptions about prior knowledge, technique links, photo/video support, error recovery, terminology variants, tips, progress checkpoints and confidence-building. Determine what an anxious or inexperienced buyer would struggle with. Feed findings into Pattern Help and PDF generation.
note: audits.BEGINNER_EXPERIENCE scores the eight things an anxious buyer meets; traps convert into checklist obligations for Pattern Help and PDF generation
title: Beginner Experience Benchmark

body: Score typography, spacing, hierarchy, photography, brand consistency, editorial polish, file naming, cover quality, navigation, hyperlinks, print-friendly options, bonus content and overall perceived value. Brambleloop's Premium Product Standard should be benchmarked against the best purchased experience, not the average.
note: audits.PREMIUM_EXPERIENCE scores thirteen elements and the standard is taken from the best purchased experience, never the average
title: Premium Experience Benchmark

body: Where purchased products include video/tutorial support, record structure, chaptering, technique coverage, pacing, correspondence to pattern sections, accessibility and whether video materially reduces ambiguity. Do not copy footage/scripts. Translate useful mechanisms into Brambleloop video requirements.
note: audits.VIDEO_TEARDOWN applies only where the manifest records video, so a pattern that never promised video is refused rather than scored zero
title: Video / Tutorial Teardown

body: Compare how competitors specify yarn, fibre, colour quantities, hooks, notions, gauge, substitutions and expected finished dimensions. Use observations to improve Brambleloop explanation and validation, not to import their design's material constants into unrelated patterns.
note: audits.MATERIALS_AUDIT compares the eight specification elements; observations improve our explanation and validation and no material constant is imported
title: Materials / Yardage / Substitution Audit

body: Record number of files, filenames, versions, print versus screen editions, charts, bonus files, language variants, file sizes and organization. Design Brambleloop's delivery bundle to be easier to understand immediately after purchase.
note: audits.DELIVERY_PACKAGING is half answered from the intake manifest (#170) and half by the analyst; the rest is refused until answered
title: Digital Delivery Packaging Audit

body: Inspect support instructions, FAQ, update policy, errata/version handling, finished-item permissions, redistribution language and contact path. Convert inconsistencies across benchmarks into a clearer Brambleloop customer experience. Legal enforceability remains subject to appropriate review.
note: audits.SUPPORT_RIGHTS scores the seven support and rights elements; legal enforceability stays subject to review
title: Support and Rights Experience Audit

body: Score each benchmark on Product Creativity, Pattern Correctness Evidence, Instruction Clarity, Chart Quality, Beginner Support, Premium Presentation, Video Support, Materials Clarity, Delivery Packaging, Support Experience, Listing Promise Alignment and Perceived Value. Preserve raw notes and confidence.
note: the twelve dimensions #161 names, scored 0-5 on a described scale rather than a feeling, with the unscored dimensions listed so a teardown that looked at two things cannot outrank one that looked at twelve.
title: Benchmark Scorecard

body: Do not copy one seller wholesale. Construct Brambleloop Premium Product Standard from the strongest mechanisms observed across the entire library: best chart practice from one benchmark, strongest navigation from another, best beginner support from another, etc., combined with Brambleloop's own engineering, version-aware support and brand system.
note: composite_standard() takes each dimension's target from whichever benchmark did it best and reports single_source until more than one contributes. Ties keep every contributor: resolving one by insertion order would bias the composite toward whatever was torn down first, which is the single-source failure arriving by accident.
title: Best-of-Breed Composite Standard

body: Benchmark parity is insufficient. For each product class, identify at least one meaningful Brambleloop advantage beyond what purchased competitors provide: stronger deterministic validation, clearer charts, better diagrams, version-aware AI help, superior print edition, colour planner, customization tool, better video, better troubleshooting or other genuine benefit.
note: check_unique_value() refuses a product class that claims no advantage beyond the composite, and the advantages are a closed list anchored in capabilities already built and checkable -- free text accepts 'better quality', which is a hope.
title: Brambleloop Must Add Unique Value

body: Competitive Teardown findings flow into the Improvement Department as structured observations. Improvement cells form hypotheses, implement in sandbox, run regression/customer-experience tests, compare against the current Brambleloop standard and promote only measurable improvements.
note: pipeline.promote() routes a finding into improve.cells.propose, so the governance boundary and the pre-change baseline both apply; pipeline.status() counts measured improvements rather than filed findings
title: Teardown-to-Improvement Pipeline

body: The library is not frozen at launch. Periodically acquire a small number of strategically selected benchmarks when a new category, unusually strong competitor, new product format or major market shift warrants it. Avoid indiscriminate spending and duplicate information.
note: benchmark refresh cadence and purchase budget; owner buys
title: Benchmark Refresh Cadence

body: Benchmark purchases are research spend. Maintain per-purchase cost, cumulative spend, research question and expected information value. Owner approval remains required above authorized spend limits. Prefer benchmarks that answer a distinct unknown rather than buying many similar products.
note: benchmark refresh cadence and purchase budget; owner buys
title: Benchmark Purchase Budget Governance

body: Competitor pattern text, charts, images and videos remain source artifacts for analysis only. Do not expose them in Brambleloop products, customer support, marketing or generated pattern content. Store derived abstractions with provenance so the company can explain what was learned without reproducing protected expression.
note: check_derived() refuses an observation that reads as a competitor's row instructions, round instructions or a transcription, and it runs on both the mechanism and the improvement text of every finding. Mechanical rather than remembered, because the moment somebody is mid-teardown with a useful paragraph in front of them is when the rule loses the argument.
title: Restricted Competitive Content Handling

body: Before live Etsy launch, select representative Brambleloop products and compare the full purchase experience against category-matched purchased benchmarks: listing promise, download packaging, PDF, charts, instructions, visual polish, support and perceived value. If Brambleloop is materially inferior on a critical dimension without a deliberate tradeoff, release is blocked for remediation.
note: pipeline.challenge() compares a product against the best category-matched benchmark on seven critical dimensions and blocks release, and launch readiness carries it as a requirement. Unrunnable until benchmarks are purchased, and products do not yet carry a benchmark category
title: Pre-Launch Benchmark Challenge

body: Add an internal question to every teardown and Brambleloop QA: 'After paying, does this feel better than expected?' Measure the mechanisms that create delight: clarity, bonus utility, navigation, polish, support, customization and confidence. Brambleloop should engineer positive surprise without bloating products with useless filler.
note: delight_question() answers 'after paying, does this feel better than expected?' from the six dimensions that actually produce that feeling and names the weakest, rather than from the mean -- a product can be average everywhere and delightful nowhere. Unscored is unanswerable, not neutral.
title: Post-Purchase Delight Metric

body: When the owner supplies purchased files, automatically generate BENCHMARK_MANIFEST.md plus a structured database import, teardown queue and gap report. Do not require the owner to manually explain every file if listing references and filenames provide enough context; ask only for genuinely missing identification. BRAMBLELOOP QUEUED MASTER UPGRADES v1.3.9 - 24/7 Cloud Autonomy, Agent Swarms & Continuous Learning This upgrade converts the owner's requirements into operational architecture: no artificial cap on specialist agents, every agent continuously improves under controlled testing, stale artifacts cannot survive upstream changes, and Brambleloop must operate autonomously in the cloud with all owner computers turned off.
note: library.scan() infers seller, file roles, counts, chart/video/print/bonus presence, sizes and hashes from filenames alone -- never opening a file -- and asks the owner only for what it genuinely cannot infer. manifest_markdown() generates BENCHMARK_MANIFEST.md, led by the sentence about what these files may never be used for.
title: Benchmark Library Manifest Deliverable

body: Every derived artifact must be tied to immutable fingerprints of the upstream evidence that created it. A CIR/design change automatically invalidates all dependent twins, geometry proofs, reverse-compiler results, certificates, PDFs, charts, visual-truth packages, listing copy, SEO, pricing assumptions, support knowledge, marketing assets and release bundles. A stable slug must never make stale output appear current.
note: CIR.fingerprint + release_hash + CHAIN_VERSION + rebuild token cover the chain (B-070/071/072); not a general content-addressed graph over every artifact class
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Content-Addressed Dependency Invalidation

body: Maintain an explicit dependency graph for every product. When any node changes, compute the exact downstream rebuild set, enqueue it idempotently, and block publication until every required descendant is rebuilt and re-certified. Store old/new fingerprints, reason, timestamp and completion evidence.
note: explicit dependency DAG with computed downstream rebuild sets
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Dependency DAG + Rebuild Propagation

body: Run a permanent sentinel that compares production artifacts against current upstream fingerprints. Any mismatch creates an incident, blocks affected publication/marketing, and triggers deterministic rebuild. Test this through deliberate stale-data injection and production restart scenarios.
note: chain.rebuild compares stored vs current and records why (B-073); not a permanent sentinel raising incidents on mismatch
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Stale-Artifact Sentinel

body: Do not impose an arbitrary small-agent architecture. The system may use dozens or hundreds of logical specialist agents/cells when parallel specialization improves quality, coverage or speed. Agent count is not a success metric: each agent must have a defined responsibility, inputs, outputs, authority, budget, quality metric and retirement condition.
note: fan-out is bounded by spend rather than by a headcount constant -- the ceiling that matters is money, and a number in the code is exactly the artificial scarcity this requirement objects to. 400 items of open work justifies fifty specialists at CA$25 remaining and eight at CA$0.40.
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Agent Abundance, Not Artificial Scarcity

body: Use an orchestrator to create or activate specialist workers based on queue depth, category, season, opportunity value and bottleneck. A large catalogue scan may fan out across many workers; quiet periods scale down. Prefer elastic logical agents over 500 permanently running paid processes when identical coverage can be achieved more reliably and cheaply.
note: capacity is computed from queue depth and deadline pressure, so a catalogue baseline fans out and a quiet Tuesday does not.
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Elastic Agent Swarms

body: Every material task, defect, opportunity, benchmark, listing, experiment, customer issue and improvement must have an accountable agent/cell and an explicit state. The orchestrator detects orphaned work and reassigns it. 'Everyone has a job' is enforced through ownership records, not assumed.
note: orphans() is a query with a name rather than a report somebody remembers to run, because unowned work is precisely the work nobody is watching.
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: No Unowned Work

body: Each agent/cell maintains a versioned capability profile: objective, baseline metrics, mistakes, lessons, successful tactics, rejected tactics, current prompt/policy/tool versions and challenger experiments. Agents regularly review their own outcomes and propose evidence-backed improvements.
note: improve/profiles.py assembles each cell's versioned capability profile from the rows rather than storing a second copy beside them: objective, metric and how it is measured, baseline and latest, promoted/rejected/reverted tactics, lessons in reach, running config versions and their challengers. A cell never measured has no capability rather than a capability of zero. self_review() proposes only from patterns in that cell's own record -- a run of three measurements the wrong way (a run is a direction, a point is weather), a metric never measured or stale past 30 days, a tactic family rejected twice for the same reason, a lesson routed here and never acted on -- and each proposal carries the rows it came from. Deterministic on purpose: a cell that writes fluent hypotheses every week looks exactly like a cell that is learning. A clean record proposes nothing and says so. Nothing here promotes: proposals enter the ordinary pipeline with its governance check, sandbox result and risk tier. /api/profiles.
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Every Agent Has a Learning Loop

body: Learning may occur continuously as evidence arrives; promotion of changes follows controlled cadence and risk tier. Low-risk scoring/prompt improvements may be tested frequently. Code, release logic, spend, policy and truth gates require regression/adversarial testing and rollback. Never equate 'constant learning' with uncontrolled production mutation.
note: improve/tiers.py grades every self-change by what it touches, never by what it is called -- a spend limit adjusted inside a change described as a scoring tweak is still a spend change, and the description is the part somebody chooses. Five tiers from scoring to gate, each with a cooldown (six changes to one surface in an afternoon cannot be attributed to anything), a rolling weekly ceiling (continuous learning with no ceiling is a company rewriting itself faster than it can observe the result) and the evidence its failure mode needs. An unknown surface grades upward to code, because defaulting downward would make 'touch something unlisted' the fast path. The gate tier -- truth gates, policy, release logic, spend, publication -- never promotes without an owner approval among its evidence. Enforced rather than offered: cells.promote() refuses an improvement that does not declare what it touches or that outruns its tier. /api/tiers.
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: High-Frequency Learning Without Blind Self-Modification

body: Create dedicated meta-agents whose sole job is to improve other agents and departments. Include evaluator, failure-miner, experiment designer, prompt/tool challenger, cost optimizer, reliability engineer, creative critic and cross-department lesson router. Their work is measured by verified uplift, not number of changes.
note: improvement swarm, agent challenger league
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Improvement Swarm

body: For important functions, maintain incumbent and challenger configurations. Replay representative historical tasks plus fresh holdouts, compare quality/cost/latency/reliability, and promote only statistically/operationally meaningful improvements. Preserve rollback and prevent test-set overfitting.
note: improvement swarm, agent challenger league
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Agent Challenger League

body: Brambleloop's core OS, scheduler, queues, workers, database, monitors and required autonomous agents must run on cloud infrastructure independent of the owner's phone, Chromebook or PC. Closing Claude, turning off the owner's computer, losing a home internet connection or sleeping overnight must not stop normal operations.
note: Railway app + embedded worker + scheduler run 24/7 independent of any owner device; verified continuously by /api/verify
