title: 24/7 Cloud Runtime Is Mandatory

body: Do not require an always-on owner PC for normal production. A local machine may be used for optional development, heavy one-off rendering, manual review or emergency recovery, but the production control plane and durable state must remain cloud-hosted. If a capability cannot yet run in cloud, surface it as an explicit integration gap rather than silently depending on the owner's computer.
note: no owner machine is production infrastructure
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Local Computer Is Not Production Infrastructure

body: A public website is not required merely to keep agents alive. The runtime needs a secure owner operations console/dashboard accessible from phone/desktop showing health, queues, products, agent activity, spend, incidents, approvals, experiments, deployment version and learning changes. This may live in the existing cloud app; do not build a public marketing site unless it has a separate business case.
note: dashboard + /api/* is the console; no approvals or learning-change view
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Website Is Optional; Operations Console Is Required

body: All recurring work uses durable cloud scheduling and leased/idempotent queues. Restarts, deploys and transient failures must not lose jobs or duplicate commercial actions. Test kill/restart/reclaim, clock drift, overlapping schedules, dead-letter recovery and exactly-once-effect behavior for sensitive actions.
note: queue/durable.py leases with idempotency keys and dead letters; test_persistence.py SIGKILLs a worker and proves recovery
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Durable Scheduler + Queue Guarantees

body: Continuously monitor worker heartbeat, scheduler freshness, queue age, DB health, external integrations, browser/vision workers, model gateways, certificate freshness and spend. Automatically restart/requeue within authority, escalate persistent incidents, and preserve evidence. 'Online' means useful work is progressing, not merely that HTTP returns 200.
note: /api/verify checks worker, scheduler, queue, DB, spend; no self-healing restart/requeue or escalation
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: 24/7 Health and Self-Healing

body: When no urgent queue exists, agents should not sit idle merely to satisfy a 24/7 slogan. They should consume a prioritized backlog: market research, competitor change detection, creative tournaments, benchmark analysis, catalogue QA, SEO experiments, learning replays, documentation, cost optimization and improvement experiments. Avoid pointless token-burning loops.
note: an idle agent takes the highest-value standing backlog item rather than polling to look alive, which spends money to produce a heartbeat, or stopping, which makes the 24/7 claim false.
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Work-Conserving Autonomy

body: Allocate autonomous capacity by expected business value and deadlines: customer incidents and truth defects first; imminent seasonal windows next; proven high-value product opportunities; listing/creative bottlenecks; experiments; background research. Prevent 500 low-value agents from starving one critical release.
note: eight priority bands, and a band is never traded away for value: a CA$5,000 opportunity with a one-day deadline does not outrank a customer incident. Deadline and value decide within a band only.
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Priority Scheduler

body: Large swarms require centralized budget control. Track cost per agent, task, product, department and experiment; enforce daily/monthly ceilings, anomaly detection and marginal-value thresholds. Scale parallelism up when it materially improves throughput/quality and down when it only duplicates work.
note: per-agent daily ceilings and SpendGuard exist; no global governor with anomaly detection or marginal-value thresholds
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Global Spend / Compute Governor

body: Competitor and market intelligence that requires traversing listings, galleries and visual assets should run from cloud-capable browser/vision workers so monitoring continues with owner devices off. Workers cache unchanged evidence, deep-audit new/changed material, respect access constraints, and preserve dated provenance.
note: cloud browser/vision worker pool -- the MJs mission gate
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Cloud Browser/Vision Worker Pool

body: Improvement agents may open bounded upgrade proposals/branches, run tests, simulations and shadow deployments, and prepare promotion evidence 24/7. Low-risk pre-authorized changes may auto-promote only within defined governance; higher-risk changes queue a concise owner approval with exact impact, cost and rollback.
note: autonomous upgrade pipeline
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Autonomous Upgrade Pipeline

body: Every department defines how often evidence should be reconsidered based on how fast its world changes. Fast-moving market/creative signals can update frequently; stable compiler mathematics need not churn hourly. The orchestrator flags stale learning, stale benchmarks and departments whose capability has not measurably improved over defined periods.
note: learning freshness SLA
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Learning Freshness SLA

body: More agents are allowed, but redundant or consistently weak agents are merged, retrained or retired. Preserve useful specialist knowledge before retirement. This prevents organizational bloat while keeping the owner's 'never too many specialists' principle focused on actual performance.
note: retirement review merges redundant cells and retires idle ones, and every recommendation carries the lessons to preserve first -- discarding what a cell learned costs more than the cell did.
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Agent Retirement / Merge Rule

body: At least once per day, run a broad improvement cycle across departments: ingest new evidence, mine failures, update candidate lessons, run challenger evaluations, identify bottlenecks, queue safe improvements and produce a machine-readable delta. Critical learning can happen sooner; nightly is the minimum comprehensive sweep.
note: nightly improvement window, weekly deep evolution cycle
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Nightly Autonomous Improvement Window

body: Run a deeper weekly audit across product creativity, pattern correctness, competitor intelligence, conversion, ads, support, infrastructure and cost. Re-evaluate department architecture itself: add specialist agents where gaps exist, merge redundant ones, revise metrics, and update the improvement roadmap.
note: nightly improvement window, weekly deep evolution cycle
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Weekly Deep Evolution Cycle

body: Before launch, prove the owner can turn off all personal computers for at least 24 hours while cloud Brambleloop continues scheduled cycles, queue processing, monitoring, learning tasks and state persistence. Record timestamps, jobs completed, incidents, costs and restart/recovery evidence. This is a launch-blocking acceptance test.
note: build2/autonomy.off_device_proof() requires jobs completed, distinct job types, completions spread across the window, scheduler activity and no unexpected dead letters. Run against production it reports four of five met on real rows
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Proof of Off-Device Autonomy

body: Any task that genuinely requires owner authorization must collapse into a mobile-friendly approval card: what is requested, why, exact capability unlocked, maximum spend, risk, rollback and consequence of waiting. Batch non-urgent approvals. Everything else continues autonomously. BRAMBLELOOP QUEUED MASTER UPGRADES v1.4.0 - Voice Session Reconciliation This is the canonical reconciliation of the critical requirements discussed in the voice session: the permanent fictional Brambleloop model, owner-directed aesthetic, identity lock, MJsOffTheHookDesigns as a permanent live benchmark, specialist intelligence pods, full-catalogue browser/vision observation, adaptive change monitoring, benchmark challenge gates and owner access approvals.
note: executor.approval_inbox() renders each unopened gate as a card with #196's seven fields, batched free-and-quick first. The asynchrony is in sync() rather than the card layout: the queue behind it does not wait
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Owner Approval Inbox

body: This section restores the owner's requirements from the voice design session into the physical master. Where an earlier requirement overlaps, this section strengthens rather than weakens it. Future references to the living master mean this actual generated artifact, not a verbally claimed version.
note: this reconciliation is canonical; recorded in the registry
title: Voice-Conversation Reconciliation Is Canonical

body: Owner requirement: develop an ORIGINAL fictional adult Brambleloop model with a highly polished, striking dark-brunette, light-eyed, high-contrast editorial beauty aesthetic, pushed strongly toward the visual qualities the owner associates with Megan Fox while remaining a distinct fictional identity rather than a duplicate of a real person's face. The system must not quietly dilute the requested aesthetic direction into a generic model.
note: canonical model: needs an image-generation capability and owner identity selection
title: Canonical Fictional Brambleloop Model - Owner Aesthetic Direction

body: Before identity lock, generate a controlled candidate set meeting the owner aesthetic: adult, long very dark brunette hair, striking light blue/green eyes, strong dark brows, high-contrast facial features, defined cheekbones, sculpted feminine jawline, full lips and premium editorial presence. Evaluate photorealism, warmth, commercial versatility, product focus, facial consistency and ability to work across seasons/categories. Owner selects the final identity.
note: canonical model: needs an image-generation capability and owner identity selection
title: Canonical Model Candidate Tournament

body: After owner selection, freeze the exact fictional model as Brambleloop's canonical recurring model. Maintain a versioned identity reference pack with approved facial geometry, hair, eye characteristics, age band, complexion characteristics and representative angles/expressions. The company may improve image quality, posing, environments, wardrobe and merchandising, but may not redesign her identity without explicit owner approval.
note: visual/identity.py holds candidates and exactly one canonical slot, and nothing moves between them without the owner. select() refuses without approval, refuses an incomplete reference pack, and refuses to replace an existing canonical identity -- approving a selection is not approving a redesign. Remaining: no candidate has been generated, because that needs the image capability.
title: Permanent Identity Lock

body: Every model-led asset must pass identity-consistency checks against the canonical reference pack. A beautiful image of the wrong woman fails. Detect gradual face drift, hair/eye drift, age drift and stylization drift across batches and over time. Failed assets regenerate before release.
note: drift_check compares against the reference pack across face, hair, eyes, age and stylisation, and an unmeasured dimension counts as maximum drift rather than being skipped. With no pack the verdict is 'unavailable' and blocks release -- never 'pass'. A check that passed for want of a reference would be believed. Remaining: the pack itself.
title: Model Anti-Drift Release Gate

body: The canonical model is attractive and premium but appropriately dressed for the product, season and Etsy shopping context. Garments must remain the commercial subject. Styling should resemble high-end crochet/lifestyle editorial photography, not glamour imagery that distracts from fit, texture, construction or product details.
note: canonical model: needs an image-generation capability and owner identity selection
title: Appropriate Product-First Styling

body: For model-appropriate products, generate a coherent shot plan: primary product-first hero, full/three-quarter fit, front/back/side as relevant, texture/detail, sleeve/neckline/closure/construction detail, scale/context and optional lifestyle shot. The model must increase trust, aspiration and brand recognition while preserving truthful product representation.
note: shot_plan() produces a job per frame -- hero, fit, detail, scale, construction, evidence -- rather than a target count, because #80 asks for minimum quality and a count produces filler.
title: Model Merchandising Shot System

body: Use the same canonical fictional model across appropriate clothing, accessories, seasonal holding/presentation shots and brand/editorial content so customers develop recognition. Do not force her into product categories where a clean product-only hero is commercially stronger. Product truth and category fit outrank compulsory model presence.
note: twelve product forms are product-first, and the model is not forced into them: a clean product-only hero is commercially stronger for a blanket, and product truth outranks compulsory brand recognition.
title: Model Identity Across the Store

body: Maintain a canonical registry of elite crochet-market benchmarks rather than relying on vague memory. Each benchmark records canonical URL, shop identity, categories, reason for inclusion, scan health, last baseline, last change, evidence freshness and specialist cells responsible. MJsOffTheHookDesigns is a mandatory anchor benchmark because the owner selected it as the primary quality/commercial reference.
note: intel/benchmarks.py declares the registry and core/models.Benchmark stores its observed state -- canonical URL, owner-supplied URL, mandate, categories, responsible pods, scan health and the three freshness timestamps. Seeded at boot and reconciled like the agent registry: code owns identity, the running system owns observed state. The panel is deliberately narrow (see #219): entries join it from evidence, never pre-populated.
title: Permanent Elite Benchmark Registry

body: Canonical benchmark URL: https://www.etsy.com/ca/shop/MJsOffTheHookDesigns . Store this literal reference in configuration and documentation. Validate URL health and resolution; if Etsy changes routing, resolve the shop's current canonical location without silently substituting a different seller.
note: the canonical URL is a literal in intel/benchmarks.py and in the registry table. resolve() validates health through an injected fetcher and classifies the result healthy / moved / unreachable / wrong_shop / unverified. A redirect that lands on a different seller, or on a search page, is refused and never re-points the registry -- record_resolution() follows a move and ignores a wrong_shop. No capability configured reports unverified, never healthy.
title: Mandatory MJsOffTheHookDesigns Source

body: On first successful browser/vision integration, enumerate the complete discoverable MJsOffTheHookDesigns catalogue rather than sampling only top listings. Record listing identity, category, visible pricing/sale state, merchandising format, media count/types, product family and dated evidence. Coverage gaps must be explicit.
note: intel/observe.py enumerates the complete catalogue by pagination rather than sampling, records listing identity, category, price, sale state, media count, product family and dated evidence, and marks the first pass as a baseline. Remaining: it has never run against Etsy, because the credential does not exist; every branch is exercised against an injected reader instead.
title: MJs Full-Catalogue Baseline

body: Every discoverable benchmark listing selected for baseline/deep audit is individually opened. Capture and analyze all accessible listing gallery assets, video where accessible, title, visible description, price/sale presentation, options/variants, badges, product claims, digital-delivery positioning, cross-sell cues and other commercially relevant listing structure. Do not claim an audit occurred if only search-result thumbnails were seen.
note: the deep audit opens each new or changed listing individually and traverses its gallery, capturing title, description, price, tags, materials, favourites and per-image colour statistics. It never claims an audit from a catalogue row: audit_state only becomes 'audited' after the gallery call succeeded. Remaining: video, variants and badges, and the fact that nothing has been run against Etsy.
title: Listing-by-Listing Deep Audit

body: Browser agents must inspect the actual gallery, not merely scrape text. For every accessible image, derive non-copying commercial observations: shot type, composition, product visibility, model/product relationship, setting, scale communication, detail coverage, infographic use, typography, palette role, thumbnail readability and emotional merchandising. Preserve dated evidence/provenance.
note: every audited gallery becomes pending analysis work with a stable per-image identity, ordered newest-first because that is the order commercial value arrives in; intel/vision.py reports the backlog size and what it would cost. The observation vocabulary is closed. Remaining: no image has been judged, because no model provider is configured -- and record() refuses an observation produced without looking at the image.
title: Vision-Level Gallery Analysis

body: Create independent specialist cells for the major product departments observed in the benchmark catalogue: garments/clothing, blankets/throws, stockings, ornaments/tree decor, home/decor, bags/accessories, hats/wearables, seasonal/gift products and additional categories as discovered. Each cell owns category-specific history, quality rubric, opportunity map and competitive lessons.
note: intel/pods.py defines the eight mandated specialist cells with ordered routing and a per-pod quality rubric, and BenchmarkObservation carries per-pod evidence. Remaining: each pod's opportunity map and category history are structurally present but empty until observation exists, and pod-level learning memory is #226/#177-194 work.
title: MJs Specialist Intelligence Pods

body: A central director coordinates specialist pods, deduplicates observations, identifies cross-category mechanisms, routes new benchmark releases to the correct cells, and prevents siloed learning. It maintains a company-level view of where Brambleloop is ahead, at parity or materially behind on concrete dimensions without using that as permission to copy protected expression.
note: intel/pods.Director deduplicates on content fingerprint, routes listings to the answering pod, finds mechanisms appearing across two or more pods, and computes ahead/parity/behind per concrete dimension -- with unknown, never parity, when either side has no evidence. Remaining: the company-level view is computed on demand rather than maintained, and has no evidence to compute from yet.
title: Central Competitive Intelligence Director

body: Do not wastefully re-download/reason over an unchanged full catalogue every 30 minutes. First establish complete baseline coverage. Thereafter run lightweight change detection frequently and trigger immediate deep audits for newly discovered listings or materially changed listings/assets. Periodically re-baseline to detect missed changes.
note: baseline, fingerprint-based change detection, and reconciliation: a listing that vanishes is marked withdrawn and kept, never deleted -- 'we saw this for six weeks and then it stopped' is a finding, an absent row is indistinguishable from a listing that never existed. Announced once, not on every later scan.
title: Baseline Then Change Detection

body: Monitoring frequency adapts to observed posting/change behaviour, seasonal urgency and evidence freshness. During active release periods or major seasonal ramps, checks may be frequent; during quiet periods they back off. The objective is near-immediate discovery of commercially meaningful changes without pointless compute burn.
note: intel/cadence.py adapts the interval from recorded change rate, consecutive quiet scans and seasonal proximity, moving one step at a time so it cannot oscillate. Deliberately asymmetric: a busy shop speeds it up immediately, a quiet one only after four consecutive empty scans, because being too slow during a release run misses the event the mission exists to catch while being too fast costs calls the fingerprint already makes nearly free. History is read from recorded scans, so a restart does not reset it.
title: Adaptive Monitoring Cadence

body: A new MJs listing becomes a structured market event. Archive dated observations, classify category, notify relevant specialist pods, decompose the commercial mechanisms, update category benchmark standards, run opportunity analysis and decide whether it justifies an original Brambleloop concept tournament.
note: a new listing becomes a structured event: archived with dated evidence, classified into a pod, routed, and turned into queued work through the coverage gap queue. Remaining: mechanism decomposition and the concept tournament it should trigger.
title: New-Listing Event Pipeline

body: Brambleloop is allowed to enter the same broad/generic product arena when market evidence supports it - e.g., cardigan, stocking, blanket, hat, ornament or coaster. Agents should identify what makes the benchmark compelling and design a substantively original Brambleloop alternative with stronger product engineering, styling, usability, fit, construction, creativity or customer experience. Do not restrict Brambleloop merely because an elite competitor also sells that generic product type.
note: same-arena response lane, breakthrough response lane
title: Same-Arena Response Lane

body: In parallel, benchmark releases should trigger a more divergent tournament asking what the competitor has NOT made: adjacent functions, new recipients, transformations, silhouettes, construction systems, bundles, seasonal stories and collection families. Maintain both incremental market participation and breakthrough exploration.
note: same-arena response lane, breakthrough response lane
title: Breakthrough Response Lane

body: Store reusable lessons only at the mechanism level: silhouette strength, fit strategy, styling, colour architecture, photography coverage, product family logic, beginner support, seasonal timing, thumbnail clarity, merchandising, bundle logic and customer promise. Do not turn competitor protected pattern text/images into Brambleloop source designs.
note: lessons are stored only against a closed mechanism vocabulary, and pods.lesson() refuses a note carrying a competitor's row-by-row instructions, chart or pattern text. The refusal is at the point of writing rather than at a review nobody schedules.
title: Benchmark Mechanism Decomposition

body: For relevant categories, place Brambleloop candidates beside current category-matched MJs benchmark evidence in a blinded comparison. Evaluate concept desirability, distinctiveness, product clarity, thumbnail strength, styling, apparent craftsmanship, giftability and purchase confidence. If Brambleloop looks obviously generic/amateur by comparison, return it to creative development rather than shipping.
note: MJs challenge gate; needs MJs evidence
title: MJs Challenge Gate

body: MJs is the anchor, not the only teacher. Maintain a changing elite panel including other category leaders and purchased Benchmark Library products. A category specialist should learn from the best available examples across sellers so Brambleloop can combine best-of-breed mechanisms and avoid overfitting to one shop's aesthetic.
note: elite panel beyond one seller
title: Elite Panel Beyond One Seller

body: When MJs or another elite benchmark materially improves presentation, product format or customer experience, relevant Brambleloop standards are re-evaluated. The competitive bar is dynamic. Improvement Department records which standards changed and why.
note: benchmark quality bar moves
title: Benchmark Quality Bar Moves

body: The MJs/elite benchmark observation layer requires production-capable browser traversal plus image/gallery understanding that operates in cloud infrastructure with owner devices off. Build 2 must not silently replace this with static seeded data, occasional manual screenshots or text-only search. Missing capability is an explicit owner/integration gate.
note: the cloud browser/vision capability is the thing being requested, so it cannot be built without it; parked on the browser_vision gate rather than counted as executable
title: Mandatory Cloud Browser + Vision Capability

body: Prove end-to-end capability against the canonical benchmark: resolve shop URL; enumerate catalogue; open multiple listings; traverse gallery assets; capture visible listing text/commerce metadata; produce image-level observations; classify into specialist pods; persist evidence; detect a simulated/new change; and trigger a re-audit. Evidence must show each step actually occurred.
note: the browser/vision acceptance test cannot run without the capability it tests; parked on the browser_vision gate
title: Browser/Vision Acceptance Test

body: The owner has stated willingness to approve reasonable access required to implement mandatory benchmark browser/vision observation and 24/7 autonomy. Claude must present any required connection, service, credential, paid infrastructure or permission as a concise approval request with exact purpose, capability unlocked, expected/max cost, security scope and consequence of declining. Never interpret willingness as blanket authorization for unbounded spend or credentials.
note: launch/access.py states every required credential or service as a structured AccessRequest carrying exact action, purpose, capability unlocked, security scope, max cost, a monthly ceiling, minutes, consequence of declining and what continues regardless. A recurring cost without a ceiling cannot be constructed, which is the blank cheque this requirement forbids. The requests join the one consolidated owner queue through launch.readiness, keyed so a re-run restates rather than duplicates. tests/test_access.py.
title: Access Approval Protocol

body: If Etsy access, anti-bot controls, authentication, tooling limitations or other constraints prevent the mandated depth of observation, report the exact limitation and preserve the requirement as unmet. Do not claim 'continuous MJs scanning' based on search snippets or stale cached evidence.
note: access.accept_evidence() grades every piece of benchmark evidence and refuses to let a substitute close a mandate, and etsy_public.capability_report() states, per mandate element, what the sanctioned API covers and what it does not -- with a proposed compliant alternative for each gap and no gap left unaccompanied. The rendered page is recorded as unmet rather than approximated.
title: No Silent Downgrade

body: Cache content fingerprints and analysis so unchanged listings are not repeatedly paid for in model/browser compute. New images, changed descriptions, pricing/sale shifts, new video or new listing identity invalidate only the necessary analysis nodes and propagate lessons through the dependency graph.
note: gateway/routing.py caches analysis on a content fingerprint that includes the routed model, so unchanged evidence is never paid for twice and a routing change cannot silently keep serving a better model's answers. A cached answer ledgers zero cost rather than recording tokens nobody spent.
title: Competitor Evidence Cache

body: Every MJs/category pod participates in the continuous-learning architecture from #177-194: maintain category mistakes, new mechanisms, successful Brambleloop responses, failed responses, current benchmarks and challenger strategies. The pod should become measurably more discerning and creative over time.
note: specialist pod continuous learning
title: Specialist Pod Continuous Learning

body: No agent may treat 'match MJs' as the final creative objective. The benchmark establishes a commercial quality floor and a source of market evidence. Brambleloop's Creative Department must still search for original white space, new product forms and stronger customer value beyond what the benchmark currently offers.
note: competitive learning is input, not creative ceiling
title: Competitive Learning Is Input, Not Creative Ceiling

body: Until automated creative evaluation has demonstrated reliable alignment with the owner's standards, the owner retains veto over canonical model identity and flagship creative quality. Repeated veto reasons become structured training/evaluation evidence for the Improvement Department rather than disappearing as chat feedback. BRAMBLELOOP QUEUED MASTER UPGRADES v1.4.1 - CA$5K/Month Scale Architecture Primary commercial objective: materially increase the probability of reaching a sustainable CA$5,000/month run rate. This upgrade expands Brambleloop from product/search excellence into a diversified acquisition, offer, retention and portfolio-growth machine. A 75%+ confidence claim remains evidence-gated, not promised by architecture alone.
note: owner quality veto with structured veto memory
title: Owner Quality Veto

body: After launch validation, the commercial operating target is a sustainable CA$5,000/month gross-revenue run rate with positive contribution economics. The system must decompose this into multiple feasible combinations of qualified visits, conversion, AOV, repeat purchase and external/direct sales, then identify the binding constraint weekly.
note: scale/target.py holds the target as arithmetic rather than a slogan: seven scenarios decomposing CA$5,000 into orders, AOV, required qualified visits, repeat share and off-platform share, each carrying gross AND contribution after Etsy's transaction fee, payment processing, listing fee and refunds. binding_constraint() ranks the five numbers by share of what the balanced scenario needs, because a 400-visit gap and a 0.4-point conversion gap are not comparable as differences.
title: CA$5K/Month Becomes the Primary Commercial Scale Target

body: Do not claim >=75% modeled confidence of reaching/sustaining CA$5,000/month merely because the architecture is sophisticated. Require multiple independent selling SKUs, positive contribution, stable quality/refund/support metrics, repeatable qualified traffic, observed conversion over meaningful samples, at least two viable acquisition loops or one exceptionally strong loop with backup, and downside scenario analysis. Display assumptions and sensitivity.
note: scale/confidence.py cannot report >=75% on architecture. Every rung counts rows; observed rates are shrunk toward the pessimistic prior by sample size; everything measured from orders is bounded by the ledger's order count, so a caller cannot argue the model upward with counts from systems that do not exist yet; and the #275 gate caps the figure at 0.74 until six evidence counts are met. Today, against 15 certified patterns and zero customers, it reports 0.0 and says no amount of further building moves it.
title: 75% Confidence Is an Evidence Gate

body: Design the catalogue so CA$5K does not require one viral hit. Maintain a base of evergreen earners, seasonal earners, flagships, quick-makes, bundles and experimental shots. Track concentration: revenue share of top 1/top 5 SKUs, seasonal concentration and channel concentration. High concentration triggers diversification while preserving winner exploitation.
note: growth/portfolio.py measures role mix against a healthy range and names the roles absent entirely, and concentration reports the SKU the company depends on. An empty portfolio has undefined concentration rather than perfect diversity -- a divide-by-nothing reports perfect health for a shop with no products.
title: Revenue Portfolio Architecture

body: Assign each SKU a portfolio role: HERO traffic/revenue driver, CORE reliable evergreen/seasonal earner, ENTRY low-friction acquisition product, BUNDLE/AOV builder, CROSS-SELL attachment product, EXPERIMENT learning vehicle or RETIRE candidate. Product creation is guided by portfolio gaps rather than raw listing count.
note: seven declared roles, and an invented one is refused. Roles are declared so a gap is something the system can see, which is what lets product creation follow portfolio gaps rather than listing count.
title: Hero / Core / Long-Tail SKU Roles

body: Engineer an intentional value ladder: free/low-friction content -> entry pattern -> premium single -> mini bundle -> flagship collection -> repeat seasonal/collection purchase. Measure movement between tiers, attach rate, contribution and customer lifetime value. Avoid discounts that train customers to ignore regular pricing.
note: revenue ladder offers, bundle attach-rate engine
title: Revenue Ladder Offers

body: Continuously identify natural product combinations and test bundles/collection offers. Track bundle attach rate, incremental AOV, cannibalization and contribution. Etsy currently supports discounted bundles and targeted offers; use available mechanisms only when policy-compliant and profitable.
note: revenue ladder offers, bundle attach-rate engine
title: Bundle Attach-Rate Engine

body: Where Etsy supports and the buyer is eligible/opted-in, test abandoned-cart, favorited-item, interested-shopper and thank-you offers. Measure incremental conversion, margin and repeat purchase versus baseline; do not assume every discount is accretive. Preserve truthful regular prices and promotion rules.
note: Etsy targeted offers; needs the shop
title: Etsy Targeted-Offer Optimizer

body: Use Etsy Marketplace Insights as first-party demand/competition evidence once accessible. Allocate limited free queries by expected information gain; consider Etsy Plus only through owner approval if unlimited research has positive expected value. Store search count, listing count, related terms, trend direction, date and geography/context.
note: Marketplace Insights allocator; needs the shop
title: Marketplace Insights Portfolio Allocator

body: Connect Etsy Stats search terms and traffic sources to listing visits, orders, revenue, contribution, support/refund and repeat purchase where data permits. Keyword strategy should optimize profitable customers, not impressions alone.
note: search-term P&L, conversion cohorts, share-of-opportunity; machinery buildable, needs real stats
title: Search-Term-to-P&L; Attribution

body: Maintain conversion baselines by category, price band, traffic source, season, shop maturity and listing age. Diagnose listings against comparable cohorts. Etsy itself defines conversion as orders divided by visits and notes photos, price, reviews, titles/descriptions and policies can affect it; Brambleloop tests those factors systematically.
note: search-term P&L, conversion cohorts, share-of-opportunity; machinery buildable, needs real stats
title: Conversion Cohort Benchmarks

body: For each target micro-market, estimate available buyer demand from first-party/observed evidence, Brambleloop qualified impressions/visits, conversion and resulting revenue. Rank opportunities by expected incremental contribution from improving visibility, CTR, conversion or offer rather than by vanity rank.
note: search-term P&L, conversion cohorts, share-of-opportunity; machinery buildable, needs real stats
title: Search Share-of-Opportunity Dashboard

body: Do not make all products compete for 'crochet pattern'. Build clusters around specific intent, recipient, season, technique, object, aesthetic, skill level and use case. Etsy query matching uses titles/tags/descriptions/categories/attributes; maximize relevant coverage without keyword stuffing.
note: commerce/search.py scores tag coverage and gaps; no query portfolio diversification across intent/recipient/season clusters
title: Query Portfolio Diversification

body: Every important launch ships with a pre-registered experiment plan: hero variants, price hypothesis, title/tag strategy, bundle/cross-sell, content/Pinterest support and success/failure thresholds. Avoid changing many variables simultaneously without recording confounders.
note: every launch ships four pre-registered experiments with hypothesis, metric, design, success and failure lines, minimum sample and stop date. An experiment with no sample floor is refused because it concludes on its first data point, and a concluded one cannot be fed more data until it says something nicer.
title: Listing Launch Experiment Pack

body: Where practical, obtain enough organic/owned traffic to estimate listing appeal before meaningful paid scaling. Ads can be used as bounded discovery, but a weak listing should not be hidden behind paid traffic. Etsy recommends allowing adequate time for Ads performance data; paid scaling decisions must respect attribution lag.
note: paid acquisition economics; needs the shop and owner-approved ad spend
title: Organic-First Proof Before Heavy Ads

body: Calculate allowable CAC from price, fees, expected refunds, discounts, repeat contribution and margin. Ads may scale only below a risk-adjusted CAC threshold with enough data. Maintain separate new-customer CAC, blended CAC and contribution after advertising.
note: paid acquisition economics; needs the shop and owner-approved ad spend
title: Paid Acquisition Allowable CAC

body: Track orders attributed to Etsy Offsite Ads separately because fee structure can materially change contribution. Use current Etsy fee/attribution rules rather than hardcoded assumptions, and incorporate any mandatory participation threshold into forecasting.
note: paid acquisition economics; needs the shop and owner-approved ad spend

body: Compare forecast versus actual weekly/monthly revenue by channel/category. Decompose error into traffic, CTR, conversion, AOV, repeat, launch timing and winner rate. Continuously recalibrate the CA$5K trajectory model; optimistic model error reduces confidence automatically.
note: revenue forecast calibration, leading indicator dashboard
title: Revenue Forecast Calibration

body: Track leading indicators before revenue arrives: qualified impressions, CTR, favourites/cart signals where available, conversion, bundle attach, email/content traffic, creator traffic, search trend direction, support defects and release velocity. Avoid declaring success from leading indicators without orders.
note: the constraint solver and loop registry expose the leading indicators that exist. Remaining: impressions, CTR and favourites, which need the shop.
title: Leading Indicator Dashboard

body: Each week, identify ONE primary commercial constraint and a small number of secondary constraints. Reallocate experiments/agents toward the constraint with highest expected marginal contribution. Examples: insufficient qualified traffic, weak thumbnail CTR, weak conversion, low AOV, low repeat or product gap.
note: the weekly constraint solver ranks the four terms by expected monthly contribution per week of effort rather than by distance from target, because the biggest gap is often the slowest to close. With every term at zero it says so plainly: the product of zeros cannot be moved by one term.
title: Weekly Growth Constraint Solver

body: Maintain a diversified experiment portfolio with expected value, cost, duration, sample requirement, owner, stop rule and result. Balance quick low-cost tests with strategic longer tests. Kill experiments that cannot change a decision.
note: experiments carry expected cost, duration, sample requirement and stop rule, and undersampled results are unclaimable rather than provisional.
title: Growth Experiment Portfolio

body: Whenever possible, distinguish incremental revenue from revenue that would have occurred anyway. Use holdouts, staggered rollouts, pre/post controls or channel attribution. Do not credit a discount, ad or creator with all observed sales merely because it was active.
note: the design decides what may be claimed: holdout and staggered rollout support a causal claim, pre/post does not -- it cannot separate the change from the week it happened in, and seasonality is the largest effect in this business. Recorded as association, in the record rather than in a caveat.
title: Incrementality Discipline

body: Shift product and marketing capacity based on time-to-event and make-time. Early season favors complex flagships; late season favors quick makes, giftables and digital last-minute projects. Roll capacity forward before demand collapses.
note: seasonal capacity arbitrage
title: Seasonal Capacity Arbitrage

body: Where Etsy data and policy permit, distinguish Canada, U.S. and other meaningful buyer markets for terminology, holidays, timing and pricing/currency effects. Do not assume Canadian search behavior represents Etsy globally.
note: finance/books.py works in CAD with Etsy fees; no cross-border lens or multi-currency normalization
title: Cross-Border Demand Lens

body: Normalize product economics into a canonical reporting currency while preserving transaction currency, platform/payment fees, regulatory/currency conversion fees and ad fees. Pricing decisions use net contribution, not sticker price.
note: scale/target.py normalises Etsy's USD listing fee into CAD at a stated assumed rate and computes contribution after transaction fee, payment processing and refunds. Remaining: preserving transaction currency per order and ad fees, which need real orders.
title: Currency / Fee Margin Normalization

body: Model loss of the top SKU, top seasonal event or top traffic channel. If CA$5K collapses under one plausible failure, create a diversification plan. Breakout exploitation remains aggressive, but resilience becomes part of the confidence score.
note: three plausible single failures -- top SKU, top family, top three -- each with the shortfall it would leave against the target. Exploiting a winner stays aggressive; this measures what losing it would cost, so resilience is part of the confidence rather than an afterthought.
title: Revenue Concentration Stress Test

body: Maintain a registry of growth loops with evidence strength: Etsy organic, Pinterest, Google/SEO, creators, email/repeat, paid ads, bundles/cross-sells, free tools/content. Record cost, latency, scalability, contribution and confidence. CA$5K confidence rises as independent loops become proven.
note: growth/loops.py registers seven loops with derived strength: untested, attempted, measured, repeatable. Strength is earned from recorded traffic rather than assigned, only measured and repeatable count as evidence, and a strength claimed on twelve visits is refused. The CA$5K acquisition rung now reads this registry rather than taking a caller's number.
title: Inventory of Proven Growth Loops

body: Before aggressively scaling a product/channel, require product quality stable, support/refunds acceptable, truthful creative certified, contribution positive or intentionally bounded, attribution working and capacity to handle resulting customer support. Growth cannot outrun product truth.
note: six scale conditions, all required. A product that converts well and generates support tickets is ready to be fixed, not scaled -- scaling multiplies whatever is already true.
title: Scale Readiness Gate

body: Maintain multiple transparent scenarios, e.g. 250 orders x CA$20 AOV, 200 x CA$25, 167 x CA$30, plus mixed Etsy/direct/repeat compositions. Derive required visits from observed conversion and include fees/refunds/ads for contribution. The CEO chooses the most evidence-supported path, not the prettiest spreadsheet.
note: the scenario matrix is computed, sorted by the traffic each path needs, and every row records whether its conversion rate was observed and over what sample. Evidence-supported paths are counted separately and today the count is zero -- with the note saying the most attractive row is the one to distrust, because it is attractive on account of its assumptions rather than its difficulty.
title: $5K Scenario Matrix

body: Track: product-quality confidence -> demand confidence -> conversion confidence -> acquisition confidence -> AOV confidence -> repeat confidence -> portfolio resilience. The modeled probability cannot exceed the weakest critical layer without explicit justification.
note: the ladder is a minimum over the critical layers, never an average: an average lets six strong rungs hide one fatal one, and 'we can make it, price it and nobody buys it' is exactly that shape. Tested with a company strong everywhere except acquisition -- the average reads above 0.7 and the model reports 0.0.
title: $5K Confidence Ladder

body: A >=75% internal modeled probability for sustainable CA$5K/month requires at minimum: several independently selling products across more than one product family; a meaningful sample of real outside customers; stable low defect/refund/support severity; positive contribution after known fees; repeatable qualified acquisition; observed bundle/AOV behavior; some repeat purchase evidence or a robust substitute; seasonal/evergreen balance; and downside scenarios that remain near the target. Thresholds adapt to actual data rather than being gamed.
note: the evidence standard is six counts (selling SKUs, product families, outside customers, orders, acquisition loops, months of history) and the modelled figure is capped at 0.74 until all six are met. Tested both ways: unmet caps a maximal ladder, and met allows a genuinely high number, because a model that can only ever report near zero would stop being read.
title: 75%+ $5K Evidence Standard

body: Once real sales exist, create a permanent CEO/CFO/Growth/Product war-room view showing current monthly run rate, 30-day forecast, gap to CA$5K, primary constraint, top five actions by expected incremental contribution, experiments in flight, winner alerts, risk concentration and owner approvals. Agents execute from this board continuously. BRAMBLELOOP QUEUED MASTER UPGRADES v1.4.2 - Proven-Trend Seasonal Capture & Lead-Time Engine NON-NEGOTIABLE owner requirement: aggressively learn from proven benchmark product markets and visual merchandising, transform those opportunities for upcoming seasons/holidays, and release early enough that customers can buy AND physically make the project before the intended event. Brambleloop independently engineers its patterns and creates its own listing assets.
note: CA$5K war room; needs real sales
title: $5K War Room

Proven demand is an instruction to compete, not a reason to avoid the category. The system should enter the same broad/generic product market aggressively while engineering Brambleloop's own pattern and producing its own visual assets.
note: proven-trend capture depends on MJs observation
title: NON-NEGOTIABLE: Proven-Trend Seasonal Capture

Browser/vision pods extract silhouette, proportions, neckline, sleeve treatment, stripe/blocking logic, colour architecture, styling, setting, product scale, shot sequence, seasonal cues and apparent customer promise. These observations feed concept generation. Do not copy the competitor's actual photograph or reproduce protected pattern instructions.
note: visual listing intelligence; needs browser/vision
title: Visual Listing Intelligence Is a Product Input

Examples include changing palette, styling, motif vocabulary, trim, gift context, collection story and supporting accessories for Christmas, Halloween, Easter, Valentine's, Mother's/Father's Day where relevant, fall, winter, spring, summer and other evidence-supported events. Transformations must remain technically coherent and commercially desirable.

title: Seasonal Transformation Engine

note: seasonal transformation engine, colour-forecast layer
title: Colour-Forecast Layer

Decompose why the product appears commercially strong, generate Brambleloop responses for the current and upcoming seasonal windows, run Creative Supremacy/benchmark gates, engineer the selected original pattern through CIR, generate Brambleloop-owned assets, then launch/advertise according to evidence.
note: MJs-to-Brambleloop response pipeline; needs MJs evidence
title: MJs-to-Brambleloop Seasonal Response Pipeline

body: A proven broad concept such as a cropped V-neck button-front striped crochet cardigan may trigger Brambleloop variants for upcoming demand: Christmas palettes (e.g. forest/cranberry/cream/gold), winter palettes, spring palettes, fall palettes and other evidence-supported themes. Preserve commercially useful generic characteristics while Brambleloop independently engineers construction, grading and instructions and creates its own model-led photography.
note: worked transformation example (striped cardigan)
title: Example Transformation - Striped Cardigan

body: Seasonal demand planning must work backward from when the CUSTOMER needs the finished object, not merely the holiday date. Estimate project make-time distribution by product/skill level, buyer planning/shopping lead time, tester/QA time, Etsy indexing/learning time, creative production time and advertising ramp. Complex products must launch substantially earlier than quick makes.
note: make-time is an interval (seasonal/uncertainty.py) rather than a point estimate; the spread is asymmetric, narrows only with recorded physical samples, and never collapses to a point
title: Maker Lead-Time Is Mandatory

body: For every event, compute: EVENT DATE minus customer completion buffer minus estimated make time minus purchase/planning buffer minus marketplace discovery/ramp buffer = target latest effective launch date. Also calculate preferred launch date with additional learning/optimization time. Recompute as observed buyer behavior improves estimates.
note: the backward chain now carries optimistic and pessimistic launch dates, and feasibility() grades a window as comfortable/tight/high-risk/infeasible with infeasible reserved for a passed optimistic bound
title: Seasonal Launch-Date Compiler

body: Classify products by customer make-time: QUICK (hours/1-2 days), SHORT (several days), MEDIUM (roughly 1-2 weeks), LONG (multi-week), FLAGSHIP (potentially many weeks). Seasonal scheduling gives LONG/FLAGSHIP products the earliest runway and can continue QUICK products much closer to the event.
note: the five lanes with make-hour bands, and the runway ordering falls out of the arithmetic rather than being imposed: a flagship's make time pushes its latest launch earlier by construction.
title: Complexity-Based Seasonal Lanes

body: Maintain a continuously rolling calendar rather than separate one-off 'Christmas strike teams.' Every day, look 30/60/90/120/180/365 days ahead for holidays, seasons, gifting moments and cultural/market events relevant to crochet. Each event has research, concept, engineering, test, asset, launch, optimization and late-season quick-make phases.
note: seasonal/calendar.py rolls: an event that has passed is next year's, so Christmas is 364 days away on Boxing Day rather than vanishing for eleven months. All six horizons index into one event list rather than duplicating it, and each event carries the phase its distance implies -- research, concept, engineering, test, assets, launch, optimise, late quick make, closed. The phase boundaries come from the lead-time engine's arithmetic, not from taste.
title: Rolling 365-Day Opportunity Calendar

body: Create persistent or on-demand specialist strike teams for major commercially relevant events. Christmas, Halloween, Easter and major seasons receive deep dedicated coverage; additional events are created when demand evidence supports them. Teams own opportunity maps, product gaps, colour/motif language, deadlines, benchmark changes and revenue targets.
note: seasonal/teams.py gives Christmas, Halloween and Easter standing teams and requires recorded demand evidence -- rows in the learning radar or observed listings, counted against a floor -- before any fourth event earns one, because a team is cheap to create and expensive to staff. A team is a share of capacity or it is a name: shares are checked against what exists, a team holding nothing is refused as an org-chart entry, and 25% is reserved for evergreen work because a seasonal programme that consumes everything leaves a shop excellent in December and absent in February. Overlapping occasions scale proportionally rather than overrunning, keeping the order the compression programmes established. A team whose occasion has passed the buyer's last practical make date releases its capacity automatically, which is how the next occasion gets staffed without a manual rebalance, and a priority programme with neither a team nor a recorded reason is refused. /api/seasonal/teams.
title: Seasonal Strike Teams by Event

body: Do not reduce an event to one blanket. For each major event, explore the full maker/gift ecosystem: garments, stockings, ornaments, tree/table decor, wreaths, coasters, baskets, pillows, throws, bags, hats, accessories, amigurumi, quick gifts, bundles and other technically/market appropriate categories. Portfolio selection remains evidence-driven.
note: depth is measured against the departments an event actually spans rather than against a product count, because six Christmas products say nothing about whether five are blankets. seasonal/depth.py turns each gap into a brief: the forms that serve the department, the make lane each form implies, whether that lane can still launch for this event, the family roles it would fill and the last optimistic launch date. A department whose forms are all past their window is reported as next season's gap rather than this season's work, and hurry is kept apart from stop. A brief is not a product: nothing here counts as coverage, and depth moves only when something is built. /api/seasonal/depth.
title: Holiday Portfolio Depth

body: Products should form coherent collections where useful. A winning seasonal visual language can extend across multiple original products and price points, enabling cross-sell and bundle behavior. Collections share palette/story but each product must stand on its own commercially.
note: seasonal/collections.py checks coherence and originality as opposing constraints, which is what makes this more than a naming convention. Members must carry the collection's palette and story, because that is what a buyer recognises across a grid; and they must differ structurally, measured by the concept engine's own distance() -- which scores a pure recolour at zero because palette is not a term in it, so a derivative is refused by the same arithmetic that refuses a duplicate in a tournament field. The closest pair is reported rather than the mean: one derivative pair makes a derivative collection and an average hides it. A collection needs three members (two is a product and its accessory) across at least two make lanes, because cross-sell is the commercial argument and it needs somewhere cheap to enter and somewhere dearer to move to. assemble() builds the largest coherent collection from candidates, greedy by lane breadth since that is the constraint that actually binds, and names what it rejected and why.
title: Seasonal Collection Architecture

body: Every observed trend receives an estimated half-life: flash/meme, short seasonal, recurring seasonal, multi-season fashion, or evergreen. Development effort and launch urgency depend on half-life. Do not spend flagship engineering time on a trend likely to expire before customers can finish the project.
note: every trend carries a half-life and the half-life caps the make lane it may justify: a flash trend cannot buy FLAGSHIP engineering. A refusal rather than a ranking penalty, because multi-week work on something that expires before a customer could finish it costs the window as well as the work. An unclassified trend is refused outright.
title: Trend Half-Life Classification

body: When a high-confidence trend is time-sensitive and technically simple, use a fast lane with bounded scope, deterministic validation and rapid asset production. Fast does not bypass pattern truth, IP/policy, visual truth or customer safety/quality gates.
note: seasonal/fastlane.py admits a candidate only when the evidence is confident, the trend's half-life can repay the work (the calendar's own rule, reused rather than restated), the make lane is SHORT or faster, the risk class is one the compiler verifies completely, and the product is one component, at most three colours and no technique the catalogue has never used -- because a new technique needs a physical sample and a sample is the one part of this company nobody can hurry. What the lane buys is scope, never checking. The gates it runs are the release chain's own CANONICAL_STAGES, imported rather than retyped, because a second copy of that list is exactly how the guarantee quietly stops being true; a test also scans certificate.py and asserts the constant matches the stages the chain actually appends. Product-conditional stages stay conditional on the product and never on the lane, and a release missing any owed gate is refused by name. /api/seasonal/fastlane.
title: Fast Response Lane

body: Periodically inspect proven Brambleloop evergreen products for legitimate seasonal re-merchandising opportunities: new colourways, styled photography, bundles, compatible add-ons and seasonal search positioning. Avoid unnecessary new pattern SKUs when the pattern itself is unchanged; preserve clean version/product accounting.
note: seasonal/remerchandising.py lists the five moves the requirement names -- colourway, styled photography, bundle, add-on, seasonal search positioning -- and refuses any that changes construction, form, rows, stitch counts, gauge or the release hash, because that is a new product and a different pipeline with a tournament, a compile and a physical test in it. No move increments the catalogue: a recolour presented as a launch inflates catalogue size, release rate and the apparent breadth of a collection at once. 'Proven' is a claim about sales and this company has none, so candidates are eligible rather than proven and every row says which. Remaining: styled photography and colourway renders need the image-generation capability, so the moves are reported blocked with what each waits on rather than missing from the list. /api/seasonal/remerchandising.
title: Evergreen-to-Seasonal Multiplier

body: Before launch, map each seasonal product to real buyer language from Etsy/market evidence: object + technique + recipient/use + aesthetic + season/event + skill/feature where relevant. Search strategy must reflect what buyers are already seeking while remaining accurate to the product.
note: commerce/intent.py maps a product across the six facets the requirement names -- object, technique, recipient/use, aesthetic, season/event, skill/feature -- and refuses the two ways the map becomes a description of ourselves: a facet carrying our own vocabulary (heirloom, quietly luxurious, curated), which produces phrases that look like research, and a facet made only of words that describe nothing. Object, recipient/use and season/event are required, because a query with no object is a category browse and that is where a new shop is invisible. The search-empty word list is deliberately not the creative one: 'easy' and 'gift' describe nothing in a premise and are most of what a shopper types. Every phrase is labelled assumed or observed, promoted only by a recorded Keyword or BenchmarkListing row, and the two are never blended into one ranked list. Remaining: with no benchmark credential every phrase is assumed, which the strategy states on each row. /api/search/intent.
title: Seasonal Search Intent Mapping

body: Paid acquisition for important seasonal products begins early enough to gather CTR/conversion/CAC evidence and improve creative before peak demand. Do not wait until the event is imminent to discover the thumbnail or offer is weak. Scaling follows the evidence-based CAC/ROAS controls in #242-244.
note: pre-season ad learning, winner scaling; needs ad authority
title: Pre-Season Ad Learning Window

body: If a seasonal product clears quality gates and demonstrates profitable/reasonable acquisition economics, automatically increase creative testing, supporting pins/content, cross-sells, bundles and paid budget within approved scaling bands. Escalate larger spend increases to the owner's mobile approval inbox with exact economics.
note: pre-season ad learning, winner scaling; needs ad authority
title: Aggressive Winner Scaling

body: For each major upcoming event, show days to preferred/latest launch, products by stage, benchmark gaps, search opportunities, projected customer make time, ad learning status, current seasonal revenue/run rate, winner alerts and bottlenecks. The orchestrator reallocates agents toward deadlines and expected contribution.
note: /api/seasonal is the war room and seasonal.sentinel recomputes it daily, naming the at-risk rows rather than counting them and raising a P2 for the soonest. What remains is seasonal revenue, run rate and ad learning status, each of which is a reading of commerce that has not happened. Unmeasured is not zero, so the war room reports them absent.
title: Seasonal Revenue War Room

body: If a product cannot realistically be discovered, purchased and completed before its intended event, do not launch it under a misleading seasonal premise merely because engineering is finished. Pivot it to evergreen/next-season positioning, simplify into a legitimate quick-make derivative, or hold it for the next cycle.
note: LaunchPlan.recommendation() refuses to return 'launch' once the window has closed, and returns pivot-to-evergreen, simplify-to-a-quick-make or hold-for-next-cycle with the reason. Finished engineering is not an argument: the customer cannot finish in time, and the conversion data that comes back would teach the shop the wrong lesson about the category.
title: Missed-Window Kill / Pivot Rule

body: After every major event, analyze which concepts, palettes, categories, thumbnails, search terms, prices, bundles and channels actually worked. Feed evidence into next year's calendar immediately, including when demand began/peaked/decayed and actual customer make-time/support signals.

Use it to expose unserved proven markets.

This is release-blocking. title: MJs Listing Photos Must Be Visually Studied

body: MJs photography may be used as visual market/merchandising evidence, but Brambleloop must create its own listing photographs/renders with its own canonical model, scenes and composition assets. Do not download/recolour/edit an MJs photograph and publish it as Brambleloop creative.
note: enforced at asset provenance in gates/asset_truth.py, which is the only place a file's origin is stated: a source outside camera/twin/generator/designer is ASSET_SOURCE_UNRECOGNISED, and provenance describing a downloaded, scraped, screenshotted or recoloured competitor image is ASSET_COMPETITOR_SOURCE. Both block publication.
title: Do Not Reproduce MJs Photo Assets

body: When MJs demonstrates demand in a broad/generic product arena - cardigan, sweater, stocking, blanket, ornament, bag, hat, coaster, decor or another category - the relevant Brambleloop pod MUST consider entering that same arena. It may preserve commercially useful generic characteristics visible from the finished product (e.g. cropped V-neck button cardigan, striped/color-blocked look, relaxed fit) while independently engineering the Brambleloop pattern.
note: intel/response.consider_arena() makes 'MUST consider' a recorded decision including a refusal, permits the generic characteristics of a finished object and refuses anything that only makes sense as a reference to the source
title: Same Proven Product Arena Is Mandatory to Consider

body: Every commercially meaningful MJs concept is evaluated against the rolling seasonal calendar. Ask how the broad product concept can speak to the NEXT season/holiday through colour palette, styling, trim, motif vocabulary, gift context, supporting accessories, bundles and merchandising. Christmas, Halloween, Easter and fall/winter/spring/summer are mandatory recurring lenses; other events are evidence-driven.
note: response.seasonalise() enumerates all eight mandatory lenses and reports a palette-only answer as the recolour it is
title: Seasonalize MJs-Proven Concepts

body: If MJs has a strong cropped striped cardigan listing, Brambleloop may deliberately compete with a cropped striped cardigan for the same broad buyer/search market and develop Christmas colourways such as forest/cranberry/cream/gold or other current seasonal palettes. Brambleloop independently engineers stitch counts, construction, grading and written instructions and generates Brambleloop-owned listing imagery.
note: the owner's Christmas cardigan example runs as a test fixture over #306 and #307 rather than as a special case in the code
title: Owner Example - Christmas Cardigan Response

body: MJs listing/new-change event -> specialist pod -> visual/text market decomposition -> demand/season fit -> seasonal colour/theme tournament -> customer make-time estimate -> preferred/latest launch date -> original CIR/pattern engineering -> truth/certification -> Brambleloop-owned premium assets -> benchmark challenge -> SEO/ads/content -> launch -> performance measurement -> winner scaling -> lessons back to MJs specialist memory.
note: response.PIPELINE names all fourteen stages and the gate each one must pass; a stage cannot run before its predecessor and a failed gate stops the run rather than marking it amber
title: MJs Trend-to-Season Mission Pipeline

body: MJs-inspired competitive responses must not arrive when the holiday starts. Work backward from the date customers want the FINISHED object. Include crochet make time, customer planning/purchase time, testing/QA, marketplace discovery/indexing, creative iteration and paid-ad learning. Complex garments/blankets receive materially more runway than quick ornaments/coasters.
note: the whole backward chain exists for this: complex garments and blankets receive materially more runway than ornaments because make time is a term in the subtraction. Measured against the generated catalogue on 2026-09-18: Canadian Thanksgiving is already missed for all eleven, and the largest piece's preferred Christmas launch is 2026-09-27.
title: Release Ahead of the Customer's Making Window

body: Continuously calculate days remaining to preferred and latest viable launch for every MJs-derived seasonal opportunity. Escalate at-risk opportunities, reallocate agents, simplify only when product truth permits, or defer to next season when the customer can no longer reasonably finish the project in time.
note: seasonal.sentinel runs daily, separates at-risk from merely past-preferred, and raises a correlated P2 only for windows where reallocating effort still changes the outcome -- a missed window is not an incident, because #297 already decided what happens to those and an incident per missed product per day trains everyone to ignore the channel.
title: MJs Seasonal Deadline Sentinel

body: At minimum maintain MJs-aware specialist capability for garments/clothing, blankets/throws, stockings, ornaments/tree decor, home/decor, bags/accessories, hats/wearables and seasonal/gift products, adding new pods as catalogue evidence requires. Each pod owns benchmark history, seasonal opportunity map, quality rubric, Brambleloop coverage and improvement experiments.
note: the eight named pods are permanent constants with rubrics: garments, blankets, stockings, ornaments, home_decor, bags, hats, seasonal_gift, plus a visible 'unclassified' queue so an unrecognised listing is never nudged into the nearest pod. New pods are added; none is pruned for a quiet quarter.
title: MJs Category Pods Are Permanent

body: After full baseline, perform frequent lightweight checks for catalogue/listing changes and immediately deep-audit new or materially changed listings. Adapt cadence to MJs observed release behavior and seasonal urgency. The goal is fast awareness without repeatedly paying to reprocess identical content.
note: frequent lightweight checks with adaptive cadence, and a changed listing triggers an immediate deep re-audit. Cost stays bounded because an unchanged listing opens no galleries.
title: MJs Change Detection Is High Priority

body: Every meaningful MJs product arena lacking a competitive Brambleloop response enters a prioritized gap queue scored by apparent demand, seasonal timing, search opportunity, make-time, expected contribution, creative potential and portfolio fit. The queue must distinguish 'uncovered', 'concepting', 'engineering', 'certified', 'launched', 'validated winner' and 'not pursuing + reason'.
note: intel/coverage.py holds the gap queue with all seven states the requirement names, a transition table that refuses a state the work did not pass through, and a mandatory reason for not_pursuing. Scored on the seven named components, each stored beside the score with the share of the weighting actually answered, so a confident number computed from one component cannot pass for a considered one.
title: MJs Coverage Gap Queue

body: For relevant products, compare Brambleloop's finished offer against category-matched current MJs evidence on product desirability, visual appeal, thumbnail strength, fit/proportion where applicable, seasonal relevance, pattern deliverables, clarity, value, trust and merchandising. If Brambleloop is visibly generic/amateur or materially weaker, return it to development.
note: MJs quality challenge; needs MJs evidence
title: MJs Quality Challenge Is Release-Blocking

body: All observations, Brambleloop launches, failures, owner vetoes, conversion data and customer outcomes update the MJs specialist pods' versioned learning memory. Challenger agents should repeatedly test better ways to interpret MJs market signals, generate stronger seasonal responses and improve commercial execution.
note: intel/memory.py versions every pod interpretation, moves standing only on recorded outcomes and refuses repetition as evidence; challengers win on outcomes or not at all, and superseded lessons are kept
title: MJs Mission Feeds Continuous Improvement

body: When the owner purchases approximately ten representative MJs patterns, treat them as a controlled customer-experience benchmark set: analyze organization, navigation, terminology, sizing presentation, charting, video/support integration, materials, troubleshooting and overall deliverable quality. Use lessons to improve Brambleloop's own independently created products. Do not reproduce protected pattern text/charts/instructions.
note: ten-pattern benchmark laboratory; owner purchases the patterns
title: Ten-Pattern Benchmark Laboratory

body: Owner command centre must expose MJs mission status: last successful scan, catalogue coverage, listings changed/new, gallery audit coverage, specialist pod assignments, top uncovered opportunities, upcoming seasonal adaptations, launch deadlines, Brambleloop comparison results, products launched, conversion/revenue and mission incidents.
note: the dashboard at / now carries a Build-2 command centre: coverage counts and executable remainder, MJs mission state including scan health, catalogue known versus audited, image backlog with its cost and the current cadence, seasonal windows with the at-risk rows named, the CA$5K probability and its binding layer, the creative gate's verdict on our own catalogue, improvement bottleneck and lessons acted on, and capabilities against spend. Every block is guarded: a page that fails to render because one subsystem is unhappy tells the owner nothing about the others, and fails exactly when they most need to look.
title: MJs Mission Dashboard

body: A system report that says only 'competitor scan complete' fails this mandate. Evidence must specifically identify MJsOffTheHookDesigns, timestamp, catalogue/listing coverage, what changed, which images/listings were inspected, which specialist pods received the evidence and what actions resulted.
note: every scan produces a report that names the shop, the timestamp, catalogue coverage as known versus inspected, what changed, which listings and images were inspected, which pods received it and what action resulted -- and mission.check_report() is run against it inside the pipeline, so a scan that could not produce a compliant report fails rather than files one.
title: No Generic Substitution

body: Build 2 is blocked until a production-capable demonstration uses the stored MJs URL, resolves the named shop, discovers listings, opens representative individual listings, traverses accessible gallery images and visible listing information, routes evidence to category pods, identifies an upcoming seasonal adaptation, computes maker-aware launch timing, produces multiple Brambleloop concept responses, and records the resulting action in the MJs Coverage Matrix. Browser/access limitations must be reported honestly rather than silently downgraded.
note: MJs end-to-end acceptance test -- blocked on browser/vision
title: MJs Mission End-to-End Acceptance Test
